 About the device
The device consists of the following components:
Conveying unit
– Conveying unit with infeed and separation belt
– Weighing conveyor
– Light barrier for package identification
– Two-part or one-part conveyor belts
– Optionally active package guidance for different packages
– Quick clamp device for simple removing of belts for cleaning purposes
– Conveying direction depending on design of device
Weighing system
– Integrated load receptor under the weighing belt
Labeling station
The labeling station is a separate unit with conveying frame, labeling belt and labeler. Sev-
eral labeling stations can be set up in a row for multi-labeling. The following labeling sys-
tems are available:
– Air-jet labeler for labeling from top or bottom
– Rotary arm labeler for labeling from top, side or front
– Piston labeler for labeling from top or bottom
– Belt labeler for labeling from bottom
Label printer in labeling system

title: Intended use
text:
The device is designed for commercial and industrial use in multi-shift operations.
 – The device may only be used for labeling packaged products or foodstuffs.
 – It may not be used to label unpackaged foodstuffs.
 – It may only be used in industrial or commercial fields.
 – The device may not be used in potentially explosive areas.
 – The goods may only be fed to the scale using the device conveyor belts.
 – The packages need to be fed continuously to the device with regular intervals be-
 tween the packages. Packages must be arranged in such a way that the packages do
 not get pushed together on the conveyor belts of the device.
 – The packages must be positioned on the middle of the belt when they are conveyed
 over the scale. Use the appropriate package guiding device. Please contact your Bi-
 zerba trade consultant for details.
 – The device must only be transported with appropriate means of transportation and if it
 was secured accordingly.
 – No constructional modifications must be made to the device.
 – Do not stand on the device and do not use the belts as deposit station.
 – Always operate the device with the conveyor belts. Dangerous spots are accessible
 without conveyor belts.

title: Verification information
text:
The device is authorized for verifiable use. Scales that are verified to a specific calibration
area (acceleration of fall) may not be used in other calibration areas without being recali-
brated.
As per statutory conditions the device operator needs to make sure that it is only applied in
proper use , see page 30. This includes metrological requirements, especially in those ca-
ses where modifications or extensions have been made.
 Non-EC countries: Please comply with the statutory terms and condi-
 tions of the respective country.

title: First verification
text:
The year of the EC verification is found on the identification plate of the device. The verifi-
cation mark on the identification plate indicates the year of the next verification due.

title: Reverification
text:
In accordance with the national verification terms and conditions, the operator is obliged to
take heed of the appointments set for regular reverification. In Germany the validity of veri-
fication for scales is currently 2 years. The verification validity period begins when the
scales are put into circulation (installation and commissioning).

title: Operating conditions
text:
Please contact us or our competent customer service points if you have any doubts con-
cerning the practical application of these conditions.
Protection type, temperature and air humidity
The permitted values and protection type can be found on the identification plate on the
device and in the technical data.
Vibration-free installation area
Vibrations can affect measurements made by the scale. During production, avoid any vi-
brations (e. g. fork-lift truck activities) near the device.
Aligning horizontally
To ensure the precision of the scale, it is of absolute necessity that the device is aligned
horizontally.
Draft
Drafts can affect the measurements made by the scale.
 Air convection
 Free air convection must be able to form around the device in order to avoid inadmissible
 heating.
 Mains voltage
 The permitted values can be found on the identification plate on the device and in chapter
 Technical data.
 Electrical charge
 Packages may not be charged electrically when being transported to the Bizerba conveyor
 belts.
 Written permission for changes
 Modifications to the devices require our prior written consent.

title: On-site mains power supply
text:
The installation of the mains power supply for connecting to our equipment must be carried
 out in accordance with the international specifications and the regulations derived from
 them. In case of a strongly contaminated network interference suppressing measures
 need to be taken, e. g:
 – Provide separate power line to our devices.
 – Include a capacitive decoupled isolation transformer or some other interference sup-
 pressing device into the feeding lines to our devices.

title: Connecting lines to external devices
text:
All connecting lines must be in shielded conduits/cables. Running of cables parallel to
 power lines is not permitted. If this is unavoidable, a minimum distance of 0.5 m must be
 kept.

text:
The legal disposal/environmental protection terms of the respective countries apply.
Only valid for Germany!
Batteries are fitted in this device which are subject to the Battery Ordinance on the return
and disposal of used batteries and accumulators.
This ordinance requires you, as the end user, to return the device to the manufacturer or

title: Requirements imposed on operating personnel
text:
The device may only be operated by people who have been instructed in the operating
 procedure. The operating personnel must be familiar with the safety devices on the device
 and have to read and understand the safety instructions in this operating manual.
 Only qualified trade personnel or Bizerba service technicians may open
 the device components.
 Even though the device is equipped with all the required safety installations, injuries to the
 operating personnel or damage to property is possible if the safety instructions are not
 heeded.
 The statutory minimum age of the operating personnel is 14 years. Please inform yourself
 with regard to varying regulations in your own country.

text:

text: During operation different dangers for operator and/or the device can occur.

title: Automatically starting components
text:
During operation, components may automatically switch on or off.
 WARNING Automatically starting components!
 During automatic operation components can switch on and off au-
 tomatically.
 This may result in serious injuries and damage to property.
 – Wear tight-fitting clothing and hairnet.
 – Do not wear necklaces, ties etc.
 – Keep fingers and hands away from movable parts.
 – Switch off the device at the main switch before carrying out clean-
 ing and maintenance work.
 WARNING Risk of entanglement by rotating parts!
 During operation, there is a risk of entanglement by rotating parts.
 This may result in serious injuries and damage to property.
 – Wear tight-fitting clothing and hairnet.
 – Do not wear necklaces, ties etc.

title: Conveyor belts
text:
The conveyor belts can be damaged if incorrectly used.
 CAUTION Objects on conveyor belts!
 Possible damage to property due to objects on conveyor belt.
 – Do not place any objects on conveyor belts. Do not use conveyor
 belts for storage.

title: Pusher to package ejection
text:
During operation, operator may be exposed to hazards.
 WARNING Crushing and impact hazard!
 During automatic operation there is a risk of injuries due to impact
 and trapping of fingers by the pusher.
 This may result in serious hand injuries.
 – When the device is switched on, do not reach into working area of
 the pusher.
 – If necessary, install protective cover above pusher.
 – Make sure gap between pusher and conveyor belt is not more than
 4 mm.
 CAUTION Pressure of compressed air of the pusher too high!
 Risk of injury through strong push from pusher.
 – Check permissible pressure of compressed air. The permissible
 pressure is indicated on a plate at the pressure reducing valve.
 The max. force of the pusher is 75 N.
 When mounting the pusher the following needs to be observed:
 – The Pusher plate must remain above the belt body.
 – The pusher must move in parallel to the belt body. Make sure gap between pusher
 and conveyor belt is not more than 4 mm.
 – The pusher must be mounted in a way that it is in the same position after disassembly
 and re-assembly.
 – The ejected packages must be collected by a suitable collecting bin.

title: Package ejector
text:
CAUTION Pressure of compressed air of the pusher too high!
 Risk of injury due to a too high force at the flaps of the package
 ejector.
 – Check permissible pressure of compressed air. The permissible
 pressure is indicated on a plate at the pressure reducing valve.
 The permissible max. force at the flaps of the package ejector is 75 N.

text:

 ers! Mortal danger!
 The pacemaker sends no or incorrect impulses.
 – Persons with pacemakers must not be near a metal detector.

title: Automatic labeler
text:
The automatic labeler weighs and labels pre-packed goods of any type. Infeed belts trans-
 port the packages to be labeled to the respective labeler. A light barrier at the conveying
 unit identifies the packages.
 The packages can be singled between the infeed and the singling belt. During transport
 the packages are weighed on the weighinng belt with integrated scale and are then la-
 beled with one or several labels above or under the labeling belt.
 The integrated trend regulation automatically regulates the customer-side control system
 subject to the calculated average values.

title: Labeling systems
text: The device can be expanded with the following labeling systems:

title: Air-jet labeler
text:
If the labeler is equipped with an air-jet labeler, the label can be applied fully automatically
 on the upper side of the package or with one labeler to the bottom of the package. The
 printed label is conveyed to the suction plate of the air-jet labeler and held there by a vac-
 uum. When the pack to be labeled is located beneath the blast head, the label is blown
 onto the pack by a powerful air jet.

title: Rotary arm labeler
text:
If the labeler is equipped with a rotary arm labeler, the label can be applied to the top of
 the package or the front or side surface of the package. Problem-free application of the
 label to round or uneven packages is also possible, thanks to the flexible labeler arm. The
 printed label is transported to the suction surface of the labeler arm, sucked in and, after a
 360 C rotation of the labeler arm, affixed to the package.
 The vacuum required for holding the label at the suction plate, is provided by an installed
 vacuum pump on the frame.

title: Piston labeler
text:
The printed label is removed from the backing paper and is conveyed under the labeling
 piston and held there by a vacuum. A stroke cylinder moves the labeling piston to the
 package. If necessary the labeling piston turns to apply the label in rotated position. After
 labeling, the labeling piston returns to its starting position.

title: Belt labeler
text:
A belt labeler labels the packages from the bottom. The printed label is detached from the
backing paper and conveyed to the vacuum nozzles of the gripper control with the assis-
tance of supporting air. The respective vacuum nozzles of the gripper are then activated
holding the label in place. The grippers then convey the label between the labeling belts,
where it is picked up by the bottom of the package to be labeled and affixed. After labeling,
the gripper returns to its starting position.

title: Device with integrated metal detector
text:
If there is a metal detector in the conveying direction of the device, metal-containing pack-
ages can be detected and ejected with an ejector (air jet, pusher or similar).

title: Bottom labeling
text:
If a bottom labelers is installed, the packages can also be labeled from below. The settings
for bottom labeling are made via the system display and operating unit.
Do not use the bottom labeling:
– In the event of moist, dripping or dirty goods, due to soiling of the jet application head.
– For packages with a round or oval surface, e.g. sausages, as the packages might slip
 when being taken.
Labeling from bottom with air jet or stamp labeler
With this design, the printed label is applied to the bottom of the package using an air jet or
stamp labeling system. For this purpose, the conveyor belt is divided into three belts above
the labeling system with the central guide belt being interrupted for label outlet. The two
external conveyor belts can be adjusted by means of a spindle according to the different
label and package sizes. The label outlet can be adjusted to max. 100 mm x 100 mm, see
page 52.
Labeling from bottom with belt labeler
With this design, the printed label is gathered by a gripper and passed between the con-
veyor belts to the bottom of the package to be labeled. ??? By this, all label sizes ap-
proved for the device can be applied to the bottom of any package, see page 55.

title: GT-12C display and operating unit
text:
The display and operating unit are operated via a SVGA touch screen that displays the
keys depending on the function. Only those keys are displayed which work with the called
up function or which are necessary.
The software of the display and operating unit GT-12C enables the configuration of the
display and operating unit as well as the settings for a connection to other devices, see
GT-SoftControl operating instructions.

title: Multi-labeling
text:
To apply several labels to the packages within one labeling process, max. 7 labeling sta-
 tions can be integrated. For operation a connection can be established from the display
 and operating unit GT-12C to each labeler via the system bus, see page 125.
 Illustration 3: Labeling line
 Labeling versions at labeling line
 – Mulit-labeling with article, deco or campaign labels
 – Additional article information, warning note, manufacturer proof, etc. on additional la-
 bels on the packages.
 – Systems with additional top labeler can apply labels from top and from bottom, e. g for
 readable goods labeling on top of package and barcode for scanner cash register at
 bottom of package.

title: Adjusting labeler to package height
text:
To achieve a high position accuracy of the labels on the packages, the labeler must be ad-
justed in height for different package heights. Depending on the device model this can be
done through a power-driven height adjustment or by moving it manually. The min. and
max. distance a from upper edge of package to lower edge of labeler depends on the re-
spective label size and sohould not be less than 10 mm and not more than 120 mm.
The following applies:
Small label: Distance 10 - 30 mm
Large label: Distance 30 - 120 mm

The expected format of the numerical value is preset in the input window. If the presetting

title: Data for current production or saving into database
text:
Depending on functional correlation and configuration of database you can decide during
saving if the data are to apply only for the current production or if they are to be saved also
into the database. Data together with article data that are saved into database, are auto-
matically called up during article change.
 Edited parameter tables saved into the database (e.g. label data) have
 an effect on all articles to which the parameter table is allocated.
 It depends on the individual configuration of the database if savings to
 the article database are made and in functional descriptions they can
 only be taken into consideration as examples. The constantly equal pro-
 cedure is described in the following.
Table
When exiting a table and the option occurs to save it for current production or additional
saving into the database, an inquiry occurs with the following possible answers:
<yes>: Save entries only for current production.
<Yes, also in database>: Save entries for current production and also into database.
<no>: Exit function without saving entries.
<Return> or <Cancel>: Return to function without saving the entries.
Input window
If a text or numeric entry can optionally be saved only either in the current production or
into the database, you can activate field "->Database [Etc]" or "Save in database" for addi-
tional saving.

title: Histogram display
text:
The histogram display (also: horizontal bar graph) indicates the static distribution of
weights in form of nine bars. It is indicated in the display formats
<L1: Large diagr. display> and <L3: Small diagr. display>, see page 91.
 The function <Statistics: histogram> is without function in combination
 with the display and operating terminal GT-12C.
 It depends on the respective setting in GT-SoftControl if the histogram
 display is indicated or not.
 The operation of GT-SoftControl is not subject of this documentation.
 Read the operating instructions on GT-SoftControl.

title: Setting analog display
text:
The analog display indicates weights and average weight values with a needle on a scale.
Illustration 48: Example of an analog display
The needles are activated via softkeys and indicate the following weights:
 <Current nom.weight Qn> Weight of the last weighed package.
 <Mean value chckedPckg.> Average value of all packages
 checked.
 <Mean value n pckg.> Average value of a preset number n
 of last weighed packages.
If the current weight exceeds the displayed weight range, the following needles are used
for the display:
 Current weight is higher than display range.
 Current weight is lower than display range.
 The needles may lie very close to each other on the scale or may even overlap. In these
 cases the following order applies for displaying:
 – Average value of preset package number (in the front)
 – Average value of packages checked (behind it)
 – current package weight (in the very back)
 If no needle has been activated, there is no analog display.

Therefore, the data of the display-optimized statistics is not deleted automatically. Article

statistics needs to be reset manually. The values of the previous packages are released
through resetting.

title: Mode levels and passwords
text:
The access to the functions of the device is regulated through so-called mode levels. With
 passwords the mode levels can be protected against unauthorized access.
 The mode levels include functions for different responsibilities. The following mode levels
 are available:
 0 Standby Clean display, lock system.

text:
el T has been created.

text:
databases work).

 Mode level T is special. This mode level can be set as per customer's requirements inde-
 pendently from the other mode levels. The user has access to exactly the functions he re-
 quires for his work, see page 120.

 key symbol, e. g for mode level 5.

title: Managing and applying macros
text:
Macros are user procedures that have been saved. They offer the following advantages:
– Device can be operated more quickly
– You have the assurance that entries are complete
– Less operating errors by users
 – Less time required for training
 – The operator can use functions in higher mode levels
 A macro can perform the following tasks:
 – Run operating steps
 – Query inputs
 – Change numerators or values automat-
 ically
 – Switch functions
 – Set settings from a selection menu
10
 Illustration 49: Start macro menu
 You can record and run macros with the macro recorder. The status of the macro recorder
 is displayed on the screen via icons, see page 68. You start all functions that manage and
 edit macros via the macro menu.
 GT-12C display and operating unit
 – Macros saved with the display and operating unit GT-12 C, the GT-12 C saves and
 not the device. Therefore these macros are missing in a line back-up of the device.
 – Macros registered with the display and operating unit are not available when operat-
 ing the device through eService.
 – Macros registered via GT-6M display and operating unit are saved on the device and
 not on the GT-12C. Therefore these macros are not available on the GT-12C.
 If necessary, you can protect macros against unauthorized access with
 passwords.
Macros only work for the device type with which they were created.

title: Managing and using templates
text:
Individually created templates make changing or entering values easier. The template
 summarizes entries and settings that would otherwise have to be accessed by different
 softkeys.
 You save your templates under template numbers. If you need to, you can allocate a tem-
 plate to a PLU.

title: Create new template
text:
Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)
10
 <Etc> / <Templates> / <Create/edit template>
 Enter new template number and confirm, see page 77.

title: Open existing template for editing
text:
Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)

 From the template editor, open another template via<Template...> /
 <Load>.

title: Edit and save template
text:
You can edit a template as follows:
– Enter or change a template name, see page 113.
– Insert new template cells, see page 114.
– Insert existing template cells, see page 115.
– Enter or change cell properties, see page 116.
– Enter or change default values, see page 116.
– Remove template cells from template, see page 117.
Save template under same name

 <Template...>

A new template cell is initially created without a default value. If "Default from cell" is acti-

 serted, the original template cell continues to be available as a possible selection.

 fects all templates that include this template cell. It is only the modified template cell

10

title: Setting up and using Quick keyboard
text:
The quick keyboard is a keyboard tailored specially to the customers' requirements to ac-
cess functions directly. It offers the following advantages:
– Quicker and easier access to functions
– Illustration of quick keys
– Reduction of control options to what the operator really needs
The following functions can be assigned to quick keys:
– Calling up articles
– Copied softkeys
– GxNet commands for all types of settings and operation queries
– Commands for different labelers
– Template cells (individual input options, e. g. with defined limits and selection lists)
– Function keys (e. g. <Print>)
– Sublevels
– HTML pages in intranet (e. g. a page of the operating instructions)
 GxNet commands are not part of this documentation. For further infor-
 mation, please contact your specialist Bizerba consultant or Bizerba
 Service.
 The GT-SoftControl operating instructions describe how to program the
 Quick keyboard.
 Use Quick keyboard

title: Define a menu structure for softkeys
text:
In mode level T you can define softkeys in menu structures with up to eight levels. At the
 highest level you can copy up to 16 softkeys and in the lower levels up to eight softkeys,
 see page 121.
 The use of submenus provides the following advantages:
 – You can protect certain functions with a password.
 – You can copy more than 16 softkeys in mode level T.
 – You can group softkeys.
 Key programming is approved, see page 102.
 Mode level: T
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Tap the access softkey to the submenu.
 Select and confirm "Submenu".

title: Enter labeling for the softkey and confirm your input (maximum of two lines whereby a
text:
new line has to be marked by an empty space, hyphen or punctuation character).
 If you don't want to protect the submenu with a password: Select and confirm "no".
 or
 If you want to protect the submenu with a password: Select and confirm "yes".
 If necessary enter and confirm the password.
 Reenter new password and confirm it.
 The submenu is now created.
 The icon marks which softkey is the access softkey to a submenu.
 The <#> character on the softkey identifies it as being password protected.

title: Edit softkeys in mode level T
text:
The following functions are available:
– Delete soft key, see page 123.
– Block softkey, see page 123.
– Activate softkey, see page 123.
Key programming is approved, see page 102.
Delete copied softkey
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the softkey you want to delete.
 Select and confirm "Delete softkey".
Block the copied softkey
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the softkey you want to block.
 Select and confirm "Deactivate softkey".
The blocked softkey is gray and cannot be used.
Reactivate blocked softkey
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the blocked softkey.
 Select and confirm "Activate softkey".
The softkey is available again for use.

title: Display softkey properties
text:
You can display the following softkey properties in mode level T:
– Position of softkey in menu
– Type of softkey (lower level/copied softkey)
– Activation status (active/passive)
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 To show a softkey's properties, simply press the softkey.
 Select and confirm "Show softkey properties".

title: Copy macros to soft key
text:
A macro recorded in mode level T can be copied to a softkey and subsequently started by
 this softkey.
 Mode level: T
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the empty softkey you want to copy the macro to.
 Select and confirm "Macro".
 Press the key that is assigned with the macro.
 The softkey is labeled with the macro name. The key and macro icon assigned to the mac-
 ro are displayed via the macro name. If the macro is protected by a password, the softkey
 also includes the "#" character.

title: Copy the customer-specific input cell to the softkey
text:
You can copy the input cells that you defined for templates to softkeys.
10
 Mode level: T
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the empty softkey you want to copy the input cell to.
 Select and confirm "Custom-spec. input cell".
 A selection list appears with the input cells defined in the templates.
 Select and confirm input cell.
 If the input cells were saved as multiple types or variants: Select and confirm variant.
 The softkey is assigned with the input cell. The value and name of the input cell appear on
 the softkey.

title: Copy operating connection to other devices on softkey
text:
If several devices are connected to your operating and display unit, you can copy an oper-
ating connection to a connected device on a softkey. Via the softkey you can switch to the
operation of a different device.
 Define an operating connection softkey on another device that subse-
 quently links to the device that was originally used. This enables you to
 switch back to operation of the originally used device.
Mode level: T
 Press <2nd.> and <Record>.
 Press the empty softkey you want to copy the operating connection to.
 Select and confirm "Device change".
 Enter and confirm the system bus address of the device to which you want to estab-
 lish an operating connection.
 Enter and confirm how you want to name, or label, the softkey.
The system bus address and the softkey label you entered now appear on the softkey.
The softkey establishes an operating connection with the respective device.

text:
With this function, you can have the manuals concerning your device shown on the
 screen. You can select from the manuals on your system in the current operating lan-
 guage.

text:
Navigate through the manual page with the help of the scroll bar and arrow keys. These
keys can be used to move to different pages:
 <Forward>
 Browse forward.
 <Back>
 Browse back.
 <Back>
 Show last displayed page.
 <Forward>
 Move to page before use of <Back> Return to displayed page.
 <Home>
 Show table of contents of manual.
 <Enter>
 End function.

The following functions are available to make targeted searches through pages in the
manuals. They can be found at the beginning of each page:
"Index": No function.
"Bookmark": Open table of contents.
"Pages": Open directory of all page numbers in manual.
"Text": Switch to text view without pictures and formatting. Use <Back>
 to return to normal view.

title: Organize article data
text:
PLU number (also: article number)
Article data can be entered in article data tables. The article data tables can be saved un-
der PLU numbers (PLU = parameter look up) and - depending on configuration - customer
numbers.
Administrating articles with reference to product group
The product group number can be saved under article data. The prices and weight per
product group are added via the product group number concerning the prices and weights
per product group that can be printed on a totals label per product group.
Administrating articles with reference to customer number
If you wish products to be labeled differently depending on the customer, then activate the
customer number by presetting the number of digits, see page 135. Then the article data
of a PLU number can be saved under different customer numbers. To call up an article the
PLU and customer number need to be entered with this configuration.
Modular structure of the article data
The article data have a modular structure. The modular structure makes it possible to use
the created data for different articles. The following data can be saved under parameter
numbers in respective database tables and assigned to the articles.
– General texts, see page 176
– Variable date texts, see page 184
– Tables static texts, see page 177
– Label parameters, see page 200
– Weight class parameters, see page 310
– Code structure rule

title: Article configuration
text:
The following settings are possible:
 – Select arity of PLU and customer number, see page 135
 – Select PLU change mode, see page 135
 – Release or disable article call-up via keyboard, see page 136
 – Release or disable automatic change with article call-up, see page 136
 The configuration of the database is not subject of this documentation.
 For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizer-
 ba Service.

title: Select arity of PLU and customer number
text:
These functions are used to define the arity of the PLU and customer number. You can
deactivate using the customer number to access a PLU if you like by applying the "Without
customer number" setting.
At least two places are needed for the PLU and customer number (if activated).
It depends on the configuration of the underlying number key how many digits can be set
in maximum. The number key can be set in an alphanumeric way with up to 20 digits or in
a numeric way with up to 9 digits.
 The configuration of the number key is not subject of this documenta-
 tion. For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or
 Bizerba Service.
Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU number>
 Select the number of digits and confirm.
 The set number of digits appears on the softkey.
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <Customer number>
 Select the number of digits and confirm.
 The set number of digits appears on the softkey.

title: Select type of PLU change
text:
You can influence the sequence of the input fields when calling-up article. The following
settings are possible:
<PLU number>: When accessing a PLU, enter PLU number first. Standard set-
 ting.
<Customer number>: Enter customer number first when calling up article.
<W. cust.-no preset>: The customer number entered at last, occurs automatically dur-
 ing article call-up. Only if article is to be labeled for a different
 customer, the customer number needs to be entered again.
Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU change> / <PLU-Mode change>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Release or disable article call-up via keyboard
text:
The following settings are possible:
 "Disabled": Article change via keyboard has been disabled.
 "Permitted": Article change via keyboard is permissible.
 "Permitted with autom. The article change via the keyboard is only permissible when
 stop": device stops.
 Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU change> / <PLU-Mode change> /
 <PLU change via keyboard>
 Select setting and confirm.
 The current setting appears on the softkey.

text:
With the following functions you define whether various automatic PLU changes can be
 completed based on PLU data:
 Weight type change: <Weight type change>

text:
Label type change: <Label type change>

 As well as the change options described here you can configure wheth-
 er the weight class and labeling type are changed with the PLU, see

text:
Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)

title: Opening article for processing
text:
The article can be saved in the database as follows:
– only under one PLU number
– under a fixed combination of PLU and customer number
The article call-up for labeling as well as the article call-up for processing, both depend on
the configuration of the database. Depending on the configuration the input window of this
function varies.
The articles can be called up as follows:
– Call up via PLU number if no customer number is allocated to the articles.
– Call-up via PLU number and customer number if both numbers are required for identi-
 fication.
Depending on the configuration the article can be searched by means of the following da-
ta, see page 77:
– PLU number
– Customer No.
– Article text

or

or

title: Processing and saving article data
text:
Some PLU data are entered directly in the PLU data editor, see page 79, while other are
 allocated to the PLU via a parameter number. When entering parameters, insert this value
 "-1" in the PLU data table, if no allocation is to be performed.
 Example: "Label param. No." = "-1" means that no label parameter table is allocated to
 the PLU.
 Data that are allocated to the PLU via a parameter number can be edited by using the cor-
 responding editor.
 With function <Edit reference> you can switch to the following editors from the article data
 editor, see page 139:
 – Text editor (for all texts saved under parameter numbers), see page 167
 – Label data editor, see page 200
 – Automatic labeler data editor, see page 249
 – Trend regulation editor, see page 454
 In order to edit the following data, you should first close the PLU data editor and then open
 the respective editor via the menu tree:
 – Weight class table, see page 311
12 – Scanning rule, see page 240
 – Code structure rule, see page 214
 – Template, see page 112
 An overview of the different article data with references to the respec-
 tive pages of the documentation can be found in the beginning of the
 chapter, see page 132.

title: Search for reference target
text:
To allocate a parameter number to a PLU data attribute, you can have a list of all available
 parameter numbers displayed with the <Search reference> softkey and then apply a pa-
 rameter number from this list.
 PLU data table is open.
 The <Search reference> softkey is ready for the edited attribute.
 Place the cursor in the table row you want to allocate a parameter number to.
 Press <Search reference>.
 Click the softkey with the magnifying glass icon to display a list of available parameter
 numbers, see page 77.
 Select and confirm data record.
 Press <OK>.
 The parameter number for the selected data record is inserted as a value into the table
 row.

title: Edit reference target
text:
To edit the following reference targets, you can move directly from the PLU data table to
another editor:
– all texts:
– Label data
– Autom. labeler data
– Tendency control
The <Edit reference> softkey is made available for the change in the respective table
rows.
 Please note that changes in reference targets have an effect on all
 those PLUs that have the same parameter number.
PLU data table is open.
 Place the cursor in a table row that includes an assignment to one of the above-men-
 tioned data records.
 Press <Edit reference>.
 The respective data record table is opened for editing.
 Make your changes and save.
 Close table.
 To save the changes, answer the security check with <yes>.
The PLU data table appears again.

title: Copy reference target
text:
Changes to the reference target have an effect on all those PLUs to which the modified
 data record is allocated. If you want to change an existing parameter data record for the
 currently processed PLU only, make a copy first and then save the copy under the new
 parameter number and then make your changes.
 PLU data table is open.
 Place the cursor in the row of the table in which the reference target is to be copied
 and changed.
 Press <Create copy from reference>.
 Enter the parameter number for the copy or use the softkey, <Next availb. no.>, to
 have it set automatically, see page 77.
 If you are using a parameter number that has already been as-
 signed, you will overwrite the data saved under this parameter
 number.
 Press <OK>.
 The parameter number for the copy is assigned to the PLU attribute. Use <Edit reference>
12 to edit the copy, see page 139.

text:
PLU data table is open.

text:
With this function you can print a list of all articles created in the system on the header of

 "Article text": Printing articles by article names in alphabetic order. This op-
 tion is only available if the database has been configured ac-
 cordingly.
 "PLU number": Print articles sorted by PLU numbers in ascending order.

ber) with the necessary data, see page 136. Depending on the configuration of your device
or database the article is called up in different ways.
– manually via PLU number, see page 142
– manually via PLU and customer number, see page 142
– manually via quick keyboard, see page 119
– automatically via EDP or scanner
 If you call up the article manually via the PLU number and call up the
 customer number, if available, you can search for the article by the arti-
 cle text depending on the configuration, see page 142.

title: Search article via article text
text:
The article that is to be called up can be searched via the article text.

title: Select weight type
text:
With the weight type, you determine the unit and the number of places after the decimal
point for displaying the weight value. You can enter the weight type as follows for certain
situations:
– in PLU data, see page 132
– for the current labeling job with the function described below
The following settings are possible:
– "kg .0001"
– "kg ,001"
– "kg ,01"
– "kg ,1"
– "kg"
– "lb ,0001"
– "lb ,001"
– "lb ,01"
– "lb ,1"
– "lb"
 If you select a weight type with a different number of digits, all the
 weight values saved in the device are adjusted (fixed weight, tare,
 weight totals).
Mode level: 2
Changing a weight type is only permitted in certain scales and for fixed weight.
In the following scales types you can switch between kg and lb:
 kg lb
6/15 kg, 2/5 g 15/30 lb, 0.005/0.01 lb
15/30 kg, 5/10 g 30/60 lb, 0.01/0.02lb
Changing the weight type for the current labeling job has to be approved by Bizerba Serv-
ice.
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Weight types>
 Select and confirm weight type.
The weight type is changed for the current labeling job. The change is not saved with the
PLU data.

title: Set weight type for weight 2
text:
If you have customer labels that include two weight fields, it is possible to print a weight in
 two different types of weight. If, for example, the weight should be printed in kg in weight
 field 1, weight can be printed in lb in weight field 2.
 While the weight type in weight field 1 depends on the scales type, you can set the follow-
 ing weight types for weight 2, independent of the scales type:
 – "W/o" (no weight type, standard setting)
 – "kg .0001"
 – "kg ,001"
 – "kg ,01"
 – "kg ,1"
 – "kg"
 – "lb ,0001"
 – "lb ,001"
 – "lb ,01"
 – "lb ,1"
 – "lb"
 Mode level: 2
13 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Print weight> / <Weight 2> / <Weight type 2>
 Select and confirm weight type.
 The setting applies from the next labeling job. It cannot be applied to the PLU data and is
 not affected when the PLU changes.

title: Switch weight type change on PLU change either on or off
text:
You can determine whether the weight type for Weight 1 that is saved with the PLU is
 called up in the event of a PLU change.
 The following settings are possible:
 "With": When a PLU is changed, the weight type saved in the PLU data
 is called up (standard setting).
 "no": The weight type is not changed when the PLU is changed.
 Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU change> / <Change options> / <Weight type change>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Enter fixed weight
text:
Thi is where you can specify a fixed weight or change the fixed weight that is called up
 with the PLU data. If the fixed weight is managed in the PLU data, you can either save the
 entered value simply for the current labeling job or have it applied to the PLU data.
 Under the following prerequisites, the nominal weight, Qn, can be dis-
 played and changed for tolerance control purposes indirectly via the
 <Fixed weight> softkey:
 – "0" is entered in the weight class as the fixed weight.
 – The labeling type is <Fixed weight>.
 When a PLU is changed, in this case the fixed weight of the PLU is
 used as the nominal weight, Qn, for tolerance control.
Mode level: 2
The fixed weight can only be used in fixed weight or fixed value labeling.
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Fixed weight>
 Enter value.
 To apply the fixed weight to the PLU data, activate the "Save in database" field.
 If the field is not activated, the entered value is only used for the current labeling job.
 Press <ok>.
The current fixed weight appears on the softkey.

text:
The settings for weight printing described below only apply to the current labeling job.
They are not stored in the database.
 Weight dimension and weight representation in the display and in print
 is entered either in the label data editor or saved under a label parame-
 ter number in the database. When a PLU is called up with the respec-
 tive label parameters, these settings are loaded automatically.

title: Switch printing of e-symbol on or off
text:
The e-symbol is, according to Prepack Regulations, the international symbol for the nomi-
nal fill quantity of a prepack. Determine here whether and where the e-symbol should be
printed. The following settings are possible:
"'e'": Do not print e-symbol on standard labels. Print e-symbol on
 customer labels in the specially designed data fields. Standard
 setting.
"UP(=0)": Print the e-mark on standard labels in the unit price field. This is
 only supported in the following cases:
 – In labeling types without the unit price.
 – When the unit price is "0".
Mode level: 2
Fixed weight or fixed value labeling
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Print weight> / <'e' print in field>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Select font height for printing weight on standard labels
text:
On certain labels (see below), the weight can either be printed at a font height of 4 or
 6 mm. Set the font height you want here.
 The following settings are possible:
 "no": The weight is printed at a font height of 4 mm. Standard setting.
 "With": The weight is printed at a font height of 6 mm.
 Mode level: 2
 The specification only applies to Bizerba standard labels with a width of 68 mm or 37 mm,
 and also to the ISB 68mm label.
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Print weight> / <6 mm wgt only>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Select weight text: Fixed weight or nominal fill
text:
Determine here which text is printed over the weight in fixed weight labeling. The following
 settings are possible:
 "Fixed weight": The text "Fixed weight" is printed over the weight. Standard set-
 ting.
 "NomQnt": The text "Nom. fil. quantity" is printed over the weight.

title: Mode level: 2
text:
<Article data> / <Weight> / <Print weight> / <Weight text fix.wgt net>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Select weight text: Meat percentage or drained weight
text:
If an operating mode that includes the ingredients is set, here you can select the text to be
 printed on customer-specific labels in the field for ingredients.
 The following settings are possible:
 "MePro": The text "Meat proport." is printed in the field for ingredients
 (standard setting).
 "Drain.": The text "Drained weight" is printed in the field for ingredients.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Print weight> / <Weight text drain.wgt>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Selecting weight indication for display and print
text:
The function is described in chapter "Setting display and keyboard layout", see page 98.
 You can also enter this setting, providing the database has been config-
 ured respectively, in label parameter tables.

title: Entering tare
text:
Usually, the weight of the packaging of a PLU is saved as the tare value in the PLU data.
Providing it is configured respectively, it is subsequently called up automatically with the
PLU, see page 149.
This is where you can enter the tare weight for the current production. If necessary, you
can have your input applied to the PLU data.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Tare>
 Enter tare.
 To save the value in article data, activate field "Save in database" .
 If the field is not activated, the tare input is only used for the current production.
 Press <OK>.

title: Allow or block tare changing on PLU change
text:
Decide here if the tare weight saved for the PLU should be called up when the PLU
changes. The following settings are possible:
"W/o": No tare change on PLU change.
"With": Tare change on PLU change. Standard setting.
Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU change> / <Change options>
 Touch softkey until required setting is achieved.

title: Work out share of ingredients
text:
Depending on the configuration, you can print the difference between the net weight and
the share of ingredients of the PLU on the label, see page 150. Do this by entering the
ingredient share as a percentage or as an absolute value, see page 150.
The different is either printed in addition to the net weight or as a price-relevant weight with
the addition"Meat proport." or "Drained weight" instead of the net weight, see page 150.

title: Configure ingredient percentage
text:
Whether and how an ingredient percentage is entered and taken into consideration, is de-
 termined via the "Ingredient selection" table field in the PLU data. You can change the set-
 ting for the current labeling job. The following settings are possible:
 <W/o ingred. propor- Do not print ingredient share. Standard setting.
 tion>:
 <Ingredients in %>: Print percentage of ingredient share.
 <Ingredients absolute>: Print absolute ingredient share.
 <Ingredients in 0.1 %>: Print ingredient shares in tenths of a percentage.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Ingredient selection>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Enter ingredient share
text:
The ingredient share is usually entered in the PLU data. You can change the ingredient
 share for the current labeling job. If necessary, you can apply your input to the PLU data.
 Mode level: 2
 The function is only active if in <Ingredient selection> not<W/o ingred. proportion> is set.
13 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Ingredient proportion>
 Enter the ingredient share in the unit displayed.
 To apply the value to the PLU data, activate the field "Save in database".
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 Press <OK>.

title: Print drained weight or net weight
text:
Determine here which weight should be printed as the price-relevant weight. The setting
 applies from the next labeling job and is not influenced when the PLU is changed. The fol-
 lowing settings are possible:
 "Net": The net weight is used to calculate the price and printed as the
 price-relevant weight (standard setting). The difference between
 the net weight and share of ingredients is also printed in addi-
 tion to the price-relevant net weight.
 "Drain.": The difference between the net weight and share of ingredients
 is used to calculate the price and printed as the price-relevant
 net weight. Depending on the configuration, "Meat proport." or
 "no" is printed as an additional text, see page 148.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Weight> / <Price-relev. weight>
 Touch softkey until required setting is highlighted.

title: Enter prices
text:
Depending on the labeling type, enter either a unit price or a fixed price:
Labeling mode Fixed price Unit price
<Weight> x
<Fixed price> x
<Fixed weight> x
<Fixed value> x
Next to the unit or fixed price, you can enter a special unit price or special fixed price, see
page 152.
A special case could be labeling a calculated unit price or special unit price. In this event,
enter the end price. A unit price is recalculated from the end price and the weight. The cal-
culated unit price or special unit price can be printed on the label, see page 153.
Prices are usually entered into PLU data, see page 132. When a PLU is called up, the pri-
ces appear automatically. This chapter describes how you can change prices for the cur-
rent labeling job.

title: Select special price option
text:
Choose an option here to deal with special prices. The following settings are possible:
<Without spec. price>: It is not possible to enter a special price, see page 152. Default
 setting.
<With spec. price>: It is possible to enter a special unit price or special fixed price,
 see page 152.
<Extra spec. price>: It is possible to enter a special unit price or special fixed price.
 The special price is printed in addition to the crossed-out origi-
 nal price on suitable customer labels. Calculated unit and spe-
 cial unit prices can be issued, see page 153.
Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <Prices> / <Spec. price versions>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Enter unit or fixed price
text:
The following description refers to the special price option
 <Without spec. price>.
 If unit price splitting is switched on, a different input window appears,
 see page 155.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Unit price>
 or
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Fixed price>
 Enter value.
 How the PLU database is configured determines whether the value can be applied to
 the PLU database.
 If the value is to be applied to the PLU data, activate the field "Save in database" .
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 When saving to the database, you might have to enter a password for mode level 3
 (local) or mode level 4 (global).
 <OK>
 The entered value appears on the softkey.
14

title: Enter special price
text:
The following description refers to the special price option
 <With spec. price>.
 In this special price option, you can enter a special unit price or special
 fixed price via the <Unit price> or <Fixed price> function.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Unit price>
 or
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Fixed price>

 Enter special unit price or special fixed price.
 If the special price is greater than zero, it is printed instead of the unit or fixed price.

title: Enter parameter for special price
text:
The following description refers to the special price option

 dition.
 – Enter additional special unit price. If the special unit price is greater than zero, the
 PLU is labeled with the special unit price and also with the price calculated from the
 special unit price and the weight. The original price is printed represented as a
 crosse

title: Unit price splitting
text:
In the standard setting, the unit price refers to the selected weight type, for example to kg,
 see page 143. If the unit price should refer to a different quantity, you can set a different
 kind of splitting for the unit price, for example 100 g.

title: Switch on/off unit price splitting
text:
The following settings are possible:
 – "With"
 – "W/o". Default setting.
 Mode level: 5
 Unit price splitting can only be switched on if the special price option,
 <Without spec. price>, is switched on, see page 151.
 <Main menu> / <Prices> / <Unit price intervals>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Enter unit price splitting
text:
The weight type determines which unit price splitting is set. In kg-based weight types, the
following splitting options are available:
– "per unit". Default setting.
– "per 100g"
In lb-based weight types, the following splitting options are available:
– "per unit". Default setting.
– "per 1/2 lb"
– "per 1/4 lb"
Mode level: 2
Unit price splitting is switched on.
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Unit price>
or
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Fixed price>
 Enter the fixed price or unit price in the first row of the able.
 The unit price per unit is displayed in the third table row for checking purposes, inde-
 pendent of the selected unit price splitting option.
 Select unit price splitting in the second table row.
 Save table and exit, see page 85.

title: Print unit price on single labels
text:
Determine here which unit price you want to print on the single labels. The following set-
tings are possible:
<Do Not Print unit price>: Don't print unit price on single labels.
<Print unit price>: Print unit price on single labels. Default setting.
<Calculate unit price>: Print the unit price re-calculated from the predefined price and
 weight on single labels.
<Recalculate all prices>: Print the re-calculated unit price and re-calculated special unit
 price on single labels.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Unit price: print/calc.>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Print dimension and currency symbol for the unit price
text:
Select here if you want the the weight dimension and currency symbol to be printed as well
 as the Unit price.
 You can have this setting saved in label parameter tables for each label
 type, see page 200.
 The following settings are possible:
 <W/o U.Ch. CS as set>: In double price labeling, print the unit price w/o weight dimen-
 sion but with the currency symbol. In single price labeling, w/o
 the dimension and w/o the currency symbol.
 <With U.Ch. CS as set>: In single and double price labeling, print the unit price with
 weight dimension and currency symbol. Standard setting.
 <W/o U.Ch. W/o CS>: In single and double price labeling, print the unit price w/o
 weight dimension and w/o the currency symbol.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Unit price: print/calc.> /
 <UP printout U.Ch./CS>
 Press softkey with respective setting.
14 14.3.3 Print unit price on total labels
 This is where you select, if the unit price is also to be printed on the total labels. The fol-
 lowing settings are possible:
 "W/o": Don't print the unit price on total labels.
 "With": Print unit price on total labels.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Unit price: print/calc.> /
 <Unit price with total>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Print the second unit price
text:
Determine here whether the unit price should also be printed in the secondary currency.
The following settings are possible:
"W/o": Only print unit price in the first currency.
"With": Print the unit price in the second currency.
Mode level: 2
The double price labeling is activated, see page 158.
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Unit price: print/calc.> / <Print. of 2nd UP>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Configure printing of the sales price
text:
Configure here whether and how the currency unit is printed for the sales price. In curren-
cy units with large and small currency units (e.g. euro/cent) you can choose whether the
price is printed in the small or large unit.
The following settings are possible:
"W/o unit of currency": Print sales price for single price labeling w/o currency unit. In
 double price labeling, the respective currency unit is printed for
 the sales price.
"With unit of currency": Print sales price in large currency unit (e.g. euro).
"In sm. unit of currency": Print sales price in small currency unit (e.g. cent).
"Cur. unit w. space": Print sales price with a space and in the large currency unit.
"In sm.curUn w.space": Print sales price with a space and in the small currency unit.
"Automatic curr. unit": Sales prices that are smaller than the large currency unit, are
 automatically printed in the small currency unit, e.g. prices un-
 der € 1 in cent.
"Autom. curr. unit Sales prices that are smaller than the large currency unit, are
w.space": automatically printed in the small currency unit, e.g. prices un-
 der € 1 in cent. Print a space in front of the currency unit.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print sales price>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Print the currency unit for totals
text:
Determine here whether the currency units printed for price totals as well. The following
 settings are possible:
 "W/o": Don't print the currency symbol for price totals on total labels.
 Standard setting.
 "With": Print currency symbol for price totals on total labels.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print sales price> / <Curr.symbol for totals>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Print secondary price
text:
When using two currencies, the price can be printed in the second currency (secondary
 price) on the label in the price field an/or in the barcode. Printing two prices in the label's
 price field is known as double price labeling.
 Determine here whether and where the secondary price should be printed. The following
 settings are possible:
 "W/oPrintOf 2nd price": Do not print a second price. Standard setting.
 "Pr. 2nd pr. num.+code": Double price labeling: Print the secondary price as well in the
 label's price field and if necessary, in the barcode, too.
 "Pr. 2nd pr. only i.code": Only print the secondary price in the barcode.
14
 To print the secondary sales price in the barcode, the code content
 "Conv. price" has to be set in the code structure rule, see page 217.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print sales price> / <Etc> / <Print 2nd price>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Select a different font size for the places after the decimal
text:
point
You can print the digits in the price before and after the decimal point in different font
sizes. This is where you select different font sizes for the places after the decimal point.
 You will find an overview of the available font sizes in the annex, see
 page 491.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print sales price> / <Etc> /
 <Font sales pr. after separator>
 Select the font size you want from the list. In the "Same as in layout" setting, the font
 size in the current label layout for decimal places is used.

title: Print conversion rate
text:
Determine here whether the conversion rate (exchange rate from primary to secondary
currency) should be printed on the labels.
 You can also enter this setting in the PLU data, see page 132.
The following settings are possible:
"W/o": Don't print conversion rate on labels.
"With": Print conversion rate on labels.
Mode level: 2
The double price labeling is activated, see page 158.
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print.of conv.rate>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Select a position for the currency symbol
text:
Determine here whether the currency symbol is printed in front of or after the sales price or
 unit price. The following settings are possible:
 "Price print s.a.nat.cur.": Print the currency symbol in the position that is typical for the
 set country, in front of or after the price. Standard setting.
 "Price print CurSym- Print currency symbol in front of the price.
 Pref.":
 "Price print CurSym- Print currency symbol after the price.
 Suff.":
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Price print pos.cu.sym.>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Select separator
text:
Determine here whether the a dot or a comma is printed in prices as the decimal place.
 The following settings are possible:
 "Print s.a.nat.cur.": Print separator in the position that is typical for the set country.
 Standard setting.
 "Print separ. ','": Print comma as separator.
 "Print separ. '.'": Print period as separator.

title: Mode level: 2
text:
<Article data> / <Price> / <Print price> / <Print separator>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Countries and changing the country
text:
You can set two countries for labeling with the suitable currency. In single price labeling,
 the currency of the 1st country is printed, in double price labeling, the prices are printed in
 both currencies.
 Alongside numerous countries, you can select a so-called neutral country with 0 to 3 deci-
 mal places as the primary and/or secondary country. You can use the
 <Curreny Neutr. coun> function to allocate the country whose currency symbol you want to
 use to the neutral country, see page 166. If you don't allocate a country with the
 <Curreny Neutr. coun> function, no currency symbol is printed. Alternatively, you can print
 any currency symbol as a logo in text field 1 for the price, see page 210.
 As well as the various countries, you can use the following settings in the <Country> and
 <Country 2nd cur.> functions:
 "Neutral 0": Print currency of neutral country without decimal places.
 "Neutral 1": Print currency of neutral country with three places after the deci-
 mal place.
"Neutral 2": Print currency of neutral country with three places after the deci-
 mal place.
"Neutral 3": Print currency of neutral country with three places after the deci-
 mal place.
 Allocation of one of the settings "Neutral 0" to "Neutral 3" is prerequisite
 for being able to use the price rounding feature, see page 163.

title: Select primary country
text:
Select the country you are labeling for. The relevant currency is displayed for the unit price
and in the event of the respective print settings, together with the unit and sales price. As
well as numerous countries, the settings "Neutral 0" to "Neutral 3" are also supported, see
page 160.
 You can also enter the currency in the PLU data, see page 132. With
 the respective configuration, the country is also called up when the PLU
 is changed, see page 162.
Use the function described here to select the country for the current labeling. The setting is
not applied to the database.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Etc> / <Country>
 Select and confirm the setting in the list you want.

title: Select secondary country
text:
This is where you can select the secondary country for double price labeling. The related
 currency is displayed with the 2nd unit price and if the respective print settings are set,
 printing includes the 2nd unit price and sales price. As well as numerous countries, the
 settings "Neutral 0" to "Neutral 3" are also supported, see page 160.
 When the PLU database is respectively configured, you can enter the
 secondary country in the PLU data as well, see page 132 and have it
 called up when the PLU changes, see page 162.
 Using the function described below you can select the secondary country for the current
 labeling job. The setting is not applied to the database.
 Mode level: 2
 The double price labeling is activated, see page 158.
 <Article data> / <Etc> / <Country 2nd cur.>
 Select and confirm the setting in the list you want.

title: Allow or block country change on PLU change
text:
This is where you determine whether a PLU change can trigger a country change automat-
 ically. If the PLU database is configured respectively, you can enter the country and the
 secondary country in the PLU data. If you allow the PLU change to trigger a change in
14 country, and the PLU data includes a country setting, a PLU change causes the related
 country to be called up automatically, the respective currency is displayed and printed.
 The following settings are possible:
 <With>: Automatic country change possible.
 <W/o>: No automatic country change possible.
 Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <PLU> / <PLU change> / <Change options> / <Country change>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Update conversion table
text:
You should keep the conversion table updated with the conversion rates used to convert
 the currency of the primary country into the currency of the secondary country for all the
 different combinations of countries in the table. When primary and secondary countries are
 saved in the PLU data and if double price labeling is activated, see page 158,, the secon-
 dary price is automatically converted from the primary price based on the conversion rate.
 Find out what the official conversion rates are (exchange rates) from
 your bank. Fixed conversion rate have to be entered to match the pre-
 set 6 significant positions exactly. You may not leave out any positions,
 nor may you round anything up or enter any inverse values you have
 calculated yourself from the official conversion rate.
 You are responsible for entering and updating the conversion rates
 yourself. It is not monitored by the device.
14
 The conversion rate to convert the euro into another currency is speci-
 fied based on the euro. Therefore always enter "EU" for € in the "Pri-
 mary" column. The euro can still be printed as the secondary currency
 on the label.
 The conversion table can loaded via the EDP system or via a storage
 medium.
 Mode level: 4
 License "EURO" is available.

title: Swap primary and secondary country
text:
Use this function you swap primary and secondary country for selected PLUs or PLU rang-
es. The function converts the unit price in the secondary currency to the unit price in the
primary currency. At the same time, it inserts the original secondary country as the new
primary country and the original primary country as the new secondary country. From the
new primary unit price, a new secondary unit price is calculated based on the conversion
rate applicable for the combination of countries.
You can limit the PLU ranges in accordance with PLU numbers, and, providing the data-
base is configured respectively, also in accordance with the the customer numbers.
 Please note that rounding errors can be incurred if the primary and sec-
 ondary country are swapped a lot.

Country and secondary country are stored in the PLU data.
The conversion rate of the opposite country combination is included in the conversion ta-
ble.

 to run the swap.
 In the "fr.customer No." row, enter the first customer number, providing the PLU data-
 base has been respectively configured, for which you want to run the swap.
 In the "t

title: Currency of neutral country
text:
With this function you specify a country for the country settings "Neutral 0" to "Neutral 3",
 see page 160. You can specify the currency of the neutral country with 0 to 3 places after
 the decimal point.
 Even if you cannot make any allocations in this function, you can assign
 the settings "Neutral 0" to "Neutral 3" to country and secondary function.
 The price is subsequently printed with the number of places after the
 decimal point you selected, but without the currency symbol. Any cur-
 rency symbol can be printed as a logo next to the price.
 Mode level: 5
 License "PRICE_OPTIONS" is available.

following is used.
 For entering one-line texts a simple text editor is available that compri-
 ses only the functions needed to enter short texts.
The text editor can be called up directly also for the following purposes:
– enter any text and save it in the system under a text number
– edit a text saved under a text number in the system

title: Loading text into Editor
text:

 <Load>

title: Selecting character size
text:
Select a suitable character size for layout. With this function also loaded fonts can be as-
signed in addition to standard character sizes. In order to load fonts, the license "LOADA-
BLE FONTS" is required.
 For further information on loadable fonts, please contact your specialist
 Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service.
The character size description is composed as follows:
12: 12x6 - 12 - 2 - 2 - 0 (example)
12: Character size
12x6 Standard setting for height and width

title: Height of font
text:
Stretch factor height
 Stretch factor width
 Font style (0=standard, 1=bold)
An overview of the possible font sizes is attached to these operating instructions, see
page 491.
 When choosing small font sizes, take into account the minimum font
 size specified in national labeling regulations.
Text editor is open.
 Set cursor at text part from where the font size needs to be applied.
 <Character size>
 Select the font size and confirm.
The text part from where the font size applies is marked in the editor through a control
character with size specification.

title: Selecting text alignment
text:
The text can be aligned per paragraph. A respective control character appears in the editor
 at the beginning of the paragraph from where the text alignment applies. The alignment
 applies until the next alignment control characters.
 The following text alignments are possible:
 "centered"
 "left"
 "right"
 With customer labels you have the option to align the text according to the field-specific
 pre-settings of the layout-description. Please select setting "Fld attribute".
 <Alignment>
 Select alignment and confirm.
15

title: Inserting further control characters
text:
The following control characters are available:
 Frame on/off:
 Frames the text.
 Graying-out on/off:
 Prints the text in gray.
 Inversion on/off:
 White text on black background.
 Underline on/off:
 Underlines the text.
 Crossing-out on/off:
 Crosses out the text.
 Store on/off:
 Stores the text in gray.
 Boldface on/off:
 Shows text in bold.
 Tabulator:
 Sets a tabulator.
 Character distance:
 Sets character spacing to value entered, max. 255 dot.
 Line spacing:
 Increases or reduces the line distance of the following text
 around the value entered. Enter value between -128 and +127
 dot.
 Automatic line break:
 There are three settings possible.
 – "Automatic break on": Line breaks automatically at the end
 of the available text field.
 – "Automatic break off": No automatic line break..
 – "Fld attribute": Line break as per field-specific pre-setting in
 label layout.
 The control character is inserted at the beginning of the text.
 This applies for the entire text.
 All control characters entered in the text can be deleted in the text edi-
 tor, like any other characters, with key <Clear>.
 Set cursor at the place where the control character is to be inserted.
 <Add. contr. characters>
 Select control characters and confirm.
 With control characters "Character spacing" and "Line spacing": Enter value and con-
 firm.
 With "Line break": Select setting and confirm.

title: Saving text for current labeling
text:
Saving for the current labeling is only possible if the text editor is called
 up via a function, e.g. <Text 1>.
 If the text editor is opened directly, the text can only be saved in the da-
 tabase under a text number.
 The text editor was not opened directly, but via a text function.
 <Exit>
 The text editor is closed. The text appears in the softkey of the function with which the text
 editor was called up. It is used for the current labeling until a new text is entered or an arti-
 cle is changed.

title: Save text in the database
text:
You can save the text under an free or already assigned text number in the database.
15
 If you use a text number that has already been assigned, the text previ-
 ously saved under this text number is overwritten.
 Text editor is open.
 <Save>
 If mode level 1 or 2 is active: To save to the database you must register a password
 for mode level 3 (local) or 4 (global).
 Enter text number and confirm, see page 77.
 If the text number is already assigned, a security check is queried.
 To have the existing text under the specific text number overwritten, answer the se-
 curity check with <yes>.

title: Closing text editor
text:
Text editor is open.
Text editor is opened via a text function
 Close without saving: <Esc>
or
 Close with saving for current labeling: <Exit>
Text editor was directly opened

or

 The text was saved under the entered parameter number.
The text editor is closed.

title: Delete text

This function is used to delete texts that are saved under text numbers in the database.
Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)
 Mode level 3: <Text> / <Delete text local>
or
 Mode level 4: <Text> / <Delete text>

 In order to finally delete the text, reply to security query with <yes>.

This function is used to delete a certain range of texts that are saved in the database un-
der text numbers.

 Enter the text number of the last text you want to delete.
 <OK>
 In order to finally delete texts from a specified range, answer the security check with
 <yes>.

title: Print list of saved texts
text:
Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)
 <Text> / <Text No. occupied>
 A list is printed. It contains all the texts saved under text numbers in the system and also
 gives details of the date and time of creation.

title: Manage general texts
text:
When using standard labels, you can print general texts in the text fields 1 to 3. Text
 fields 1 and 2 usually contain texts about the company, the products or ingredients. The
 optional text field 3 contains, for example, special texts for promotion campaigns. You can
 print up to 20 general texts on customer labels.

 General texts can be saved in the database under text numbers and allocated to PLUs
 based on these text numbers, see page 138.
 After calling up a PLU, the general texts are displayed on the relevant softkeys <Text 1> to
 <Text 20>. General texts can be called up for editing via the softkeys.
 General texts <Text 4> to <Text 20> are only for customer labels.

Example: <Text 1>. The procedure for all other general texts is the same.

title: Save general text under a text number in the database
text:
You need the password for mode level 3 (local) or 4 (global) for the save process.
General text is opened in the text editor.
 <Save>
 If the current mode level is 1 or 2: To save to the database, enter and confirm a pass-
 word for mode level 3 (local) or 4 (global).

 If a text already exists for the text number you have entered, a security check ap-
 pears.
 To overwrite the existing text, answer the security check with <yes>.
The general text is saved under the selected text number. The change affects all PLUs to
which this text number has been assigned.

title: Manage static texts
text:
Static texts are used to allocate a set of defined texts to customers' labels. Before static
texts are created for the first time, you have to activate the required static texts in the data-
base.
 Configuration of the database is not part of this documentation. For fur-
 ther information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba
 Service.
 Static texts are saved in text tables. Depending on the configuration, a text table can con-
 tain up to 50 static texts to be printed on customer labels. Static text tables are saved un-
 der parameter numbers in the database. You can allocate these tables to PLU data or ac-
 cess them directly for labeling you are currently working on.
 Once you have opened a static text table, you can edit the individual texts for the current
 labeling job.
 Allocation of static texts to text fields on customer-specific labels is han-
 dled by a layout program, such as Bizerba Label Designer (BLD) or the
 label layout editor in GT-SoftControl. You can find more information in
 the introduction to the program you decide to use.
 The following functions are available:
 – Open table of static texts in order to edit, see page 179.
 – Edit static text table, see page 179.
 – Save static text table, see page 180.
 – Close static text table, see page 180.
 – Delete static text table , see page 180.
 – Open static text table for current labeling job, see

title: Manage date texts
text:
On blank labels or customer labels, you can print the packing date or sell-by date as either
a standard date text or as a variable date text. A variable date text for the last use-by date
is additionally available for customer labels.
Variable date texts are saved under date text numbers in the database. You can allocate
date texts to PLUs so that they are automatically accessed when the PLU changes. For
the current labeling job you may enter or change variable date texts directly.
 Date texts are only printed on labels if the related date is printed as well. In order to print
 variable date texts on date 1 and 2, set the label layout options for date text printing
 <With var. date text>, see page 183.

title: Date text field 1: Text on packing date
text: (date 1)

text:
(date 2)

 standard label
 The following functions are available:
 – Configure printing of date texts, see page 183.
 – Managing the date text in the database, see page 184.
 – Enter or change date text for current labeling job, see page 185.
 – Delete date text, see page 185.
15

title: Configure printing of date text
text:
With this function you define whether standard date texts or variable date texts are printed
in addition to the data on blank labels and customer labels. You can only use variable texts
if one of the following prerequisites is given:
– Date texts exist in the database and have been assigned to the PLU
– Date texts have been entered for the current labeling job.
The following settings are possible:
<W/o date text>: Print no date text. Setting for standard labels with preprinted
 date text. Default setting.
<With std. text>: Print standard date text for date 1 and date 2 on blank labels or
 customer labels.
<With var. date text>: Print variable date text for date 1 and date 2 on blank labels or
 customer labels.
 The date text for date 3 is not affected by this setting. There is no stand-
 ard text for date 3. If a variable date text 3 exists, this is printed inde-
 pendent of the setting.
Mode level: 2
 <Texts> / <Date texts> / <Date text printing>
or
 <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Etc> / <Date text printing>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Managing the date text in the database
text:
You can manage date texts in the database and assign them to PLUs via the date text
 number. When a PLU is changed, the assigned date text is accessed automatically.
 If you change a date text in the database, the change is applied to all
 those PLUs to which the date text is allocated.
 You can also start this function from mode level 2. Initially, the proce-
 dure is the same as entering a date text for the current labeling job, see
 page 185. If you press <Save> after editing, you are prompted to enter
 a password. After entering and confirming the password for mode lev-
 el 3 (save locally) or 4 (save globally), the continued procedure follows
 the description from Entering the Parameter Number, mentioned below.
 Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)
 <Date text> / <Date text editor>
 <Load>
 Enter and confirm date text number, see page 77.
 Edit text in the text editor, see page 167.
 <Save>
 Enter and confirm the date text number you want, see page 77.
 If a date text already exists for the entered number, a security check prompt appears.
15 If you answer <yes> the text is saved in the database under the entered number.
 Close text editor via <Exit>.

title: Enter or change the date text for the current labeling job
text:
The date text that is entered as described below applies until the next change or until a
different date text is opened, for example when the PLU is changed.
Example: Date text 1.The procedure for date texts 2 and 3 is the same.
Mode level: 2
Change date text

 Edit text in the text editor, see page 167.
