The text appears in the softkey and is used as of the next labeling job.
 If necessary, you can use this function to have entered date text saved
 to the database. Use the <Save> function in the text editor, see
 page 184.
 To save to the database you need the password for mode level 3 (save

Mode level: 3 (local) or 4 (global)
 <Date text> / <Delete date text>
 Enter and confirm date text number, see page 77.
 In order to finally delete the Date text, reply to security query with <yes>.

title: Managing PLU texts
text:
The PLU text is displayed in the text field on the display and on the labels. The article can
be searched via the article text. Usually you have to update the PLU text via the PLU data,
see page 137. The PLU text for the currently open PLU is displayed on the softkey
<Article text>.
With this function you can enter or change the PLU text for the current labeling job directly.
Mode level: 1 or 2
Edit PLU text for the current labeling job
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Texts> / <Etc> / <Article text>
or
 Mode level 2: <Texts> / <Article text>
 The current PLU text appears in the text editor.
 Process text, see page 167.
 <Exit>
 The text editor is closed. The entered text appears in the softkey and is used in the next
 labeling job.

title: Managing simple texts
text:
Simple texts consist of a single line and contain up to 15 characters. Use simple texts for
 delivery addresses, dispatch types and store names, for example, on customer-specific la-
 bels.
 Allocation of simple texts to text fields on customer-specific labels as
 well as definition of text sizes and other properties is handled via the re-
 spective customer-specific label layout.
 Enter simple texts directly in article data, see page 131. After opening an article, the sim-
 ple texts are displayed on the softkeys <Simple text 1> to <Simple text 10>. Simple texts
 can be temporarily changed for the current labeling job via the softkeys.
 Example: <Simple text 5>. The procedure for the other simple texts is the same.
 Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Texts> / <Etc> / <Simple texts 1-10> / <Simple text 5>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Texts> / <Simple texts 1-10> / <Simple text 5>
 Enter or edit text.
 <OK>
15
 The simple text appears in the softkey.
 It is immediately used for customer-specific labels to which simple text has been assigned.

title: Packed-on, sell-by and use-by date
text:
You can print three dates on labels. These are usually:
– Packed-on date (date 1)
– Sell-by date (date 2)
– Use-by date (date 3)
 Date 1 to Date 3 can be assigned differently, see page 191. For further
 information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service.
Dates are entered or calculated based on the system time. On the softkeys in the display,
calculated and entered data are told apart by parentheses:
Date in parentheses: calculated date
Date without parenthe- entered date
ses:
 Enter the last two digits of the year number only. If you need further dig-
 its, they are inserted automatically.

title: Enter date 1
text:
Usually the system date at the time the label is printed as used as the packed-on date
(date 1). No input is required here. If necessary, you can enter date 1.
Mode level: 2
Enter date 1
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Date 1>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Enter date 2
text:
The sell-by date (date 2) is usually calculated automatically from the system date and
shelf-life days 1 entered for the PLU. No input is required here. If necessary, you can enter
date 2.
Mode level: 2
Enter date 2
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Date 2>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Enter date 3
text:
The use-by date (date 3) is usually calculated automatically from the sell-by date (date 2)
 and shelf-life days 2.
 If necessary, you can enter date 3.
 Mode level: 2
 Enter date 3
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Date 3>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Shelf life days
text:
You can enter the following shelf-life days:
 Shelf-life days 1: The shelf-life days 1 serve to calculate the sell-by date (date 2)
 from the packed-on date (date 1).
 The following applies: Sell-by date = Packed on date + shelf-life
 days 1.
 Shelf-life days 2: The shelf-life days 2 serve to calculate the last use-by date
 (date 3) from the sell-by date (date 2).
 The following applies: Last use-by date = sell-by date + shelf-
 life days 2.
 Calculation of date 1, 2 and 3 can be configured differently from the de-
 scription above. For further information please contact your Bizerba
 consultant or Bizerba Service.
16 For certain types of food, the specification of half-days for sell-by and use-by are required.
 In order to enter half-days, add the value, 900, to the number of half-days. enter the value
 calculated as described when you are setting the shelf-life days 1 or 2.
 Values over 900 that are entered in the functions <Shelf- life 1> and
 <Shelf- life 2> are treated as half days.
 Example: If you use the function <Shelf- life 1> and enter one half day, you enter the val-
 ue 900+1 = 901.
 Shelf-life days are usually managed via the PLU data, see page 132. The shelf-life days
 are automatically called up on a PLU change. You can enter or change the shelf-life days
 directly for the current labeling job.

title: Enter shelf-life days 1
text:
With this function you enter the shelf-life days 1 for the current labeling job. If necessary,
you can have your input applied to the PLU data.
Mode level: 2
Enter shelf-life days 1
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Shelf- life 1>
 Enter the number of shelf-life days, or the calculated value for entering half days.
 In order to save the entered value in the PLU data for the current PLU, activate the
 "Save in database" field.
 Press <OK>.

title: Enter shelf-life days 2
text:
With this function you enter the shelf-life days 2 for the current labeling job. If necessary,
you can have your input applied to the PLU data.
Mode level: 2
Enter shelf-life days 2
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Shelf- life 2>
 Enter the number of shelf-life days, or the calculated value for entering half days.
 In order to save the entered value in the PLU data for the current PLU, activate the
 "Save in database" field.
 Press <OK>.

title: Enter time date 1, 2, and 3
text:
Instead of date 1, 2 or 3, providing the respective configuration is in place, you can print
the time, see page 190. Usually the system time is used here. You can also enter the time
manually.
Example: <Time Date 1>. The procedure for <Time Date 2> and<Time Date 3> is the
same.
Mode level 2
Enter time date 1
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Time Date 1>
 Enter and confirm time.

title: Enter + days
text:
When you set the options for printing correspondingly, instead of specifying a use-by date
(date 3), you can enter the number of days from the sell-by date the product should be
used by, e.g. "+ 5 days", see page 191. Enter the number of days you want printed for the
current labeling job instead of the use-by date.
 The + days can be entered indirectly via the sell-by date in the PLU da-
 ta. To support this feature, printing of the date is configured in such a
 way that the shelf-life days 1 or 2 are printed instead of date 3. For fur-
 ther information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba
 Service.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Set date/ time> / <Etc> / <+ days>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Print options for date 1
text:
Select here how you would like date 1 printed on the labels. The following settings are
 possible:
 <W/o print. of date1>: Do not print date 1.
 <With date1>: Print date 1.
 <Date 1 coded>: Print date 1 as calendar week.
 Example: "CW 35".
 <D.o.Y. (x) date 1>: Print date 1 as day of year without any leading zeros.
 Example: "51" instead of 20.02.
 <D.o.Y.(00x) date 1>: Print date 1 as day of year with three digits and incl. leading ze-
 ros.
 Example: "051" instead of 20.02.
16 <As a const. ->datefld1>: When printing date 1 as a day of the year with leading zeros,
 enter constant number of days (offset) that should be added to
 the day of the year.
 Example: Date: 15.01. -> Day of year: 015; offset: 10 ->
 print: 025.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Date 1 options>
 For <As a const. ->datefld1> additional, press <Etc>.
 Press softkey with respective setting.
 In the option, <As a const. ->datefld1>: Enter and confirm offset.

title: Print options for date 2
text:
Select here how you would like date 2 printed on the labels. The available settings and
 procedure are the same as for printing options for date 1, see page 190.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Date 2 options>

title: Print options for date 3
text:
Select here how you would like date 3 printed on the labels. The available settings and
procedure are the same as for printing options for date 1, see page 190.
And you can also choose from the following settings for date 3:
<With + days>: Print +days on labels instead of date 3, see page 189.
<D.o.Y. datefld3>: If a day of the year is set for date 3: Print day of year from
 date 1, 2 or 3 in date field 3.
 The following settings are possible:
 <Of date 3>: Print day of the year from date 3 in-
 stead from date 3. Default setting.
 <Of date 1>: Print day of the year from date 1 in-
 stead from date 3.
 <Of date 2>: Print day of the year from date 2 in-
 stead from date 3.
Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Date 3 options>

title: Determine format for printing date
text:
You can specify formatting for printing the date in a table. The effect of the date printout
 are shown in the last row of the table "Preview (Date 1)".
 The table combines different settings to print the date, which are also
 available as individual functions. By changing the settings in the table,
 you change the settings in the following functions (the reverse is true
 too):
 – <Date notation>, see page 193
 – <Date format>, see page 194
 – <Date: half days>, see page 195
 We recommend generally using the comprehensive function,
 <Data formatting>, instead of the individual functions.
 The following table rows are available:
 "Month notation": Select how the month should be displayed.
 Possible settings:
 – <Numeric>, e. g. "03.11.09"
 – <Alphanumeric>, e.g.. "03.NOV.09"
 – <Roman>, e.g. "03.XI.09"
 "Format": Select date format (T: position for day M: position for month, Y:
 position for year).
 Possible settings:
 – <DD.MM.YY>, e. g. "03.11.09"
16 – <DD.MM.YYYY>, e. g. "03.11.2009"
 – <MM.DD.YY>, e. g. "11.03.09"
 – <MM.DD.YYYY>, e. g. "11.03.2009"
 – <YY.MM.DD>, e. g. "09.03.11"
 – <YYYY.MM.DD>, e. g. "2009.11.03"
 – <DDMM>, e. g. "03.11"
 – <MM.YY>, e. g. "11.09"
 – <MM YYYY>, e. g. "11.2009"
 "Separator": Select a separator for date display.
 Possible settings:
 – <W/o>: Do not use any separator.
 – <. >: Use period as separator.
 – < / >: Use slash as separator.
 – < -

title: Select how to write the date
text:
This is where you select how the month is displayed and which separator is used.
The following settings are possible:
<Month Num. xx.08.xx>: Numeric display of month, period as separator.
<Month A/N xxAUGxx>: Alphanumeric display of month, no separator.
<Month A/N xx.AUG.xx>: Alphanumeric display of month, period as separator.

<Month Rom. xx.VIII.xx>: Display of month in Roman numerals, period as separator.

 <Data formatting>. If you change the setting of the <Date notation>

Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Print date/time> / <Date notation>

title: Select date format
text:
This is where you select the format you want for printing the date. The available formats
 differ in how the date parts are organized T (position for day), M (position for month) and Y
 (position for year) as well as how separators are used. The following settings are possible:
 – <DD.MM.YY Europe>
 – <MM.DD.YY U S A>
 – <YY.MM.DD>
 – <DD.MM>
 – <MM.YY>
 – <DD.MM.>
 – <DDMM>
 You can also influence the date format with the <Data formatting> func-
 tion. If you change the setting of the <Date format> function, the table
 for the <Data formatting> function is automatically adjusted.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Print date/time> / <Date format>
 Press softkey with respective setting.
16

title: Select how half-days should be displayed
text:
This is where you select how you want half-days to be displayed on labels.
The following settings are possible:
<Da.w/o haDa Display without half-days,
DD.MM.YY>: e. g. "03.11.09"
<Dat.w.haDa DD.MM V>: Display without specification of year but with half-day symbols,
 e.g. "03.11 V"
<Dat.w.haDa. Display with specification of year and half-day symbols,
DD.MM.YY V>: e.g. "03.11.09 V"
<Half-daysymbol>: The following settings are possible here:
 – V/N: "V" for morning and "N" for afternoon
 – M/A: French half-day symbols, "M" for morning (matin) and

text:
Determine here if you want the year number to be displayed as a two or four-digit num-
bers.
Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Print date/time> / <Print.of year>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Select time format
text:
Determine here how the packed-on and sell-by time is printed in the respective date fields
 of the customer labels. The following settings are possible:
 "Hours": Print hours only.
 "Hrs:Min": Print hours and minutes.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Print date/time> / <Time format>
 Tap the soft key until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Switch on/off printing time
text:
This is where you can switch printing of the time for date 1 and date 2 either on or off. The
 following settings are possible:
 "no": Do not print time.
 "With": Print time.
 Mode level: 2
 <Date> / <Print date/time> / <Select time>
 Tap the <Print of Time 1> or <Print of Time 2> softkey until the setting you want is
 visible.

title: Further print settings
text:
Further settings relevant to printing date and time can be made by Bizerba Service. These
 relate to:
 – deviation from printed reference date and system date
16 – updating reference date when switching device on

 For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizer-

title: Numbers and values
text:
The chapter describes the following numbers and values that can be saved together with
the PLU data:
– Product group number, see page 197
– Piece number per package, see page 198
– Printable numbers, see page 199
 The production numbers that are independent from the article are de-
 scribed in chapter "Enter production numbers" , see page 279.

title: Entering product group number
text:
You can assign a product group number to a PLU in order to enable evaluations according
to product groups. Product group totals can be calculated via the product group number,
see page 296.
The product group number is entered as follows:
– directly in the PLU data, see page 132
– via the function described below
If a product group number is assigned to the current PLU via the PLU data, the product
group number is called up automatically with the PLU and displayed on the softkey
<Pr. group number>.
Using the function described below you can either enter or change the product group num-
ber simply for the current labeling job, or save it under the PLU number of the current arti-
cle in the database. If you save it in the database, you must ensure that the relevant attrib-
ute is approved in the PLU database, see page 132.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Numbers + values> / <Pr. group number>
 Enter value.
 To save the value in the article data, activate field "Save in database" .
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 When saving to the database, you might have to enter a password for mode level 3
 (local) or mode level 4 (global).
 Press <OK>.
The entered value appears on the softkey.

title: Entering the number of pieces per package
text:
One piece number per package can be printed on labels for fixed price packages. This is
 done via the fixed price. The piece number per package is entered as follows:
 – directly in the PLU data, see page 132
 – via the function described below
 If a piece number per package is assigned to the current PLU via the PLU data, they are
 automatically called up together with the PLU and displayed on the softkey
 <Pieces/ package>.
 Using the function described below you can either enter or change the piece number per
 package simply for the current labeling job or save it under the PLU number of the current
 article in the database. If you save it in the database, you must ensure that the relevant
 attribute is approved in the PLU database, see page 132.
 Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Numbers + values> / <Pieces/ package>
 Enter value.
 To save the value in article data, activate field "Save in database".
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 When saving to the database, you might have to enter a password for mode level 3
 (local) or mode level 4 (global).
 Press <OK>.
 The entered value appears on the softkey.

bers are printed in the respective data fields on customer labels.

– using the function described below

cally called up together with the PLU and displayed on the respective softkey.
Using the function described below you can either enter or change printable numbers sim-
ply for the current labeling job, or save them under the PLU number of the current PLU in
the database. If you save them in the database, you must ensure that the respective attrib-
utes are approved in the PLU database, see page 132.
The softkeys <Printable number 1> to <Printable number 3> are only approved for input
when "Print only" is configured for the respective content, see page 198.
How to enter printable numbers is described based on an example of Printable Number 4.
The procedure for other printable numbers is identical.
Mode level: 2
 <Article data> / <Numbers + values> / <Etc> / <Printable num. 4-11> /

title: Manage label parameters in tables
text:
If you are working with very different labels, you can save the settings required for specific
 labels in label parameter tables. Allocate the suitable label parameter table to a PLU via
 the label parameter number. If label type changes are allowed, the label parameters as-
 signed to a PLU are automatically called up when the PLU is changed, see page 136.
 You can call up label parameter tables independently of the PLU, see page 203. All label
 settings can be changed independently of the label parameter table for the current labeling
 job.
 In devices that are operating in a system network, the attributes in the
 label parameter table can be defined locally (only for the device) or
 globally (for all the devices in the network), see page 131.
 For further information on working with the system network please con-
 tact your Bizerba sales consultant or the Bizerba Service.
18

text:
Label parameter tables are usually allocated to PLUs and automatically called up whenev-

title: Select label layout
text:
You define which label layout to use via the label type. You can also choose between the
following label types:
Standard labels: Standard label layouts according to Bizerba or ISB standards
 with varying label widths and heights.
Customer labels: Label layouts created in accordance with customer specifica-
 tions and save in the device under label numbers.
Special labels: Test label layouts that are permanently saved in the device.
Euro labels: Standard label layouts according to Bizerba or ISB standards
 with additional fields for double price labeling.
Different label types are available for selection for each label layout.
 Customer label layouts are created by using special software on a com-
 puter. In order to use them, the customer label layouts have to be cop-
 ied to the device via the serial interface or a storage medium and saved
 under a number and name. They are subsequently available as custom-
 er label types.
 How to create a customer label layout is not part of this documentation.
 For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizer-
 ba Service.
 If double price labeling is activated, instead of the selected standard la-
 bel type, the corresponding euro-label type is set automatically.
The label layout is usually allocated to the PLU via a label parameter table and set auto-
matically on PLU change. You can use this function to change the

text:

 The label size determines the height of text field 2 (PLU and ingredient text).

title: Switch 180° rotation on or off
text:
If you have labels that have to be wound in such a way that the foot of the label comes out
of the printer first, you can use this setting to rotate the label layout by 180°. The following
settings are possible:
"W/o": Do not rotate label. Default setting.
"With": Rotate label by 180°.
 These settings can also be entered in the label parameter table, provid-
 ing the database is respectively configured to do so. Subsequently they
 are automatically set when the label parameter table is called up, see
 page 201.
 If you print the customer label rotated by 180°, you have to activate re-
 verse mode, see page 393.

or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Rotation by 180°>

title: Set variable header length
text:
The variable header length is the area of the label occupied by a preprinted company
header and therefore should not be printed on. Enter the height of the preprinted company
header as the variable header length.
 These settings can also be entered in the label parameter table, provid-
 ing the database is respectively configured to do so. Subsequently they
 are automatically set when the label parameter table is called up, see
 page 201.
 A variable header length can be defined in the label layout. If you set the variable header
 length to "0" at the device directly or via the label parameter table, the variable header
 length in the label layout could take effect.
 If textfield 1, underneath the preprinted company header is empty, you
 can enter the height of the preprinted company header as the variable
 header length, minus 10 mm. Label printing subsequently starts, incor-
 porating the empty area of textfield 1.
 Mode level: 1 or 2
 Set or change the variable header length for the current labeling job
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Var. header length>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Var. header length>
 Enter and confirm value from range between 0...180 mm.

title: Set the light barrier offset
text:
The front and back edges of the label are scanned by the light barrier in order to position
 text and values as precisely as possible. In the event of irregular label shapes, the detec-
 ted label edges do not necessarily correspond to the start and end of the label. The devia-
 tion that is incurred can be offset by entering a positive or negative offset value for the
 front and back edges of the label.
 First of all, print a test label and measure the offset you will need.
 These settings can also be entered in the label parameter table, provid-
 ing the database is respectively configured to do so. Subsequently they
 are automatically set when the label parameter table is called up, see
 page 201.

title: Mode level: 1 or 2
text:
Change light barrier offsets for the current labeling job
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <LB offset front edge>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <LB offset rear edge>
 Now press <Etc> in mode level 1. Menu path continues as for
 mode level 2.
 Enter and confirm each value within a range of -450...450 dot.

title: Set line spacing
text:
With this function you can decrease and increase the line spacing in multiple-line text
fields on the label by the entered value.
Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Line spacing>
or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Line spacing>
 Enter and confirm value in dot.
A negative value decreases the line spacing and a positive value increases the space.

text:
If you are printing on to a ticket, enter the layout length in mm to be printed here. When "0"
is entered, the layout is printed at its original length.
Mode level: 1 or 2

or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Etc> / <Layout lgth ticket>
 Enter and confirm value in mm.

price.

The following settings are possible:
"W/o": Print without frame. Default setting.
"With": Print with frame.
Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Frame>
or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Frame>

– Weight text, see page 208
– Price text, see page 208

 – Total text, see page 209

text:
Decide here if you want a country-specific weight text to be printed on blank labels, see
 page 148. The following settings are possible:

 "With": Text is printed.

 <Weight text printing>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Etc> / <Texts> / <Weight text printing>

text:
Decide here if you want a country-specific standard text to be printed on blank labels for
 the sales price. The following settings are possible:
 "W/o": Text is not printed. Standard setting.
 "With": Text is printed.

 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Etc> / <Texts> /

 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Layout options> / <Etc> / <Texts> / <Price text printing>

In standard labels you can use this function to print an additional text in Text 3 on the bot-

title: Switch digit code on or off
text:
A special digit code can be printed on labels in the device number field. The three-digit
code is put together from the two-digit department number and a weighted check digit. The
check digit is formed from the maximum 6-digit selling price and the maximum 2-digit de-
partment number. If one of these specifications is exceeded, no digit code is printed.
The digit code can only be printed if no lot number and no operator number was entered.
The department number is entered as the device number, see page 278.
 The following settings are possible:
 "W/o": Print without digit code. Default setting.
 "With": Print with digit code.

 <Print> / <Digit code>

text:

 page 210. The following settings are possible:

 or

title: Codes and scanning rules
text:
You can print barcodes on labels. A data field on standard labels and up to seven data
 fields on customer labels are available. Which article data are to be printed as a barcode
 on the labels, can be defined in the code structure rules. Code structure rules can be
 saved under code structure numbers and can be allocated to the data fields in the article
 data.

title: Important terms for barcodes
text:
left bright zone: Free zone on the left of the first dark bar of the barcode. This
 bright zone may not be printed, as it is needed by the reading
 devices to identify the barcode.
 right bright zone: Free zone on the right of the last dark bar of the barcode, see
 left bright zone.
 Module width: The module width is the width of the smallest barcode bar.
 Each code-bar is generated from integer multiple of the narrow-
 est code-bar element.
 Ratio: The ratio only applies for code families with two differnt bar
 widths.
 Line for optical charac- The optical characters line is the readable layout of the code
 ters: content under the actual barcode.
 Middle check digit: The middle check digit can be selected in most codes. It is cal-
 culated based upon the code content that is behind the check
 digit (4 to 6 digits). The calculation depends on the respective
 code type.
 Manufacturer number E. g national company number (bbn), prespecified by the Zen-
 trale for Coorganisation [Head Office for Coorganization].
 Article number A unique number for an article at company level. This can be
 specified by the manufacturer.
 Code structure: Code structure: Describes how the code is put together - from
 one or more subelements. The subelements in a code can be
 flexibly combined within the framework of the maximum code
19 length. Examples of subelements are:
 – the article number
 – the

title: Manage code structure rules
text:
You enter code structure rules via the code editor and save them under code structure
 numbers in the database. Allocate the code structure rules to PLUs via the code structure
 numbers. Depending how the PLU database, the fields "Code struc. i. c.field1" to "Code
 struc. i. c.field7" are available for this purpose.
 Code structure rules contain up to 100 code contents with numeric and alphanumeric vari-
 ables such as PLU number, manufacturer or company number, price, weight, text. Code
 substrings can also belong to the code contents. Code substrings are managed with the
 PLU data and contain PLU-dependent data. The length of the code substring is dictated by
 the code structure rule.
 The code structure rules allocated to the code fields are automatically called up with the
 PLU. The following functions are available to help you manage the code structure rules:

title: EAN-D3 code
text:
The EAN-D3 code is formed from a total of 24 digits. This number of digits is binding. Only
 numeric data can be encoded. The minimum module width is 0.27 mm. The light zones
 amount to 9 modules each.
 The combinations of barcode symbols are known as Block 2 and Block 6 according to
 UPC Specifications. Block 6 is formed from the 1/2EAN8 and EAN8 symbols. Block 2 is
 represented by the EAN13 symbol. Each block is concluded by a symbol check digit. Block
 2 and block 6 can be allocated behind each other or over each other.

title: EPC-96 Code for RFID labels (UHF only)
text:
If the device is equipped with a write unit or RFID labels (Smart Label, RFID = Radio
 Frequency Identification), information can be transmitted by the transponder integrated in
 the labels.
 RFID label components and functionality
 – Transponder with antenna
 – analogue circuit for sending and receiving
 – a digital circuit for saving information
 Transponders in the labels save the transmitted data. Special scanning devices can read
 out these data without needing to make contact. The device transmits the information that
 needs to be saved at 865-920 Mhz (UHF) to the transponder.
 Prespecifications and settings when applying RFID labels
 – Activate Smart Label, see page 392
 – Create code structure rule, see page 215
 – Select code field for smart label, see page 231
 Description of the EPC-96 code
 The Electronic Product Code EPC-96 is for transmitting 96 bit data to the RFID transpond-
 er in the RFID label. The code structure is globally determined by EPC.
 The data in the code structure rule are saved as binary data in EPC-96. Data smaller than
 one byte have to be entered as binary data. All possible 96 bits of the EPC-96 code must
 be defined.
 The following examples are based on the code structure rule SGTIN-96. In SGTIN-96, the
 96 bits comprise the following:
 Header Filter Value Partition Company prefix Item reference Serial number
 8 Bits 3 Bits 3 Bits 20-40 Bits

title: Managing automatic labeler parameters in tables
text:
You may manage different automatic labeler settings in labeler parameter tables and as-
sign them to articles via parameter numbers. The settings are automatically called up
when the PLU is changed.
You can call up automatic labeler parameter tables independently from the PLU, see
page 251.
All automatic labeler settings can be changed independently from the labeler parameter ta-
ble for the current labeling job.
 In devices that are operating in a system network, the attributes in the
 automatic labeler parameter table can be defined locally (only for the
 device) or globally (for all the devices in the network), see page 131.
 For further information on working with the system network please con-
 tact your Bizerba sales consultant or the Bizerba Service.

title: Setting the height offset of the labeler
text:
The height offset compensates the height differences between air-jet, rotary, and piston la-
belers, so that the differences between the labelers must not be taken in consideration
when entering the maximum package height.
 The height offset is factory-set or set by the Bizerba service and may
 not be changed.
The motorized height adjustment for labelers is available and activated.
Mode level: 5
Modify height offset for current labeling job
 <Automat> / <Labeler> / <Offs.height labeler>
 To reduce the initial height, enter the minus sign.
 Enter the height offset in mm and confirm it.
The labeler is automatically moved. The setting is not applied to the database.

title: Setting the transverse offset of the labeler
text:
The transverse adjustment compensates the transverse offset between air-jet, rotary, and
piston labelers with regard to the conveying direction, so that the differences between the
labelers must not be taken in consideration when entering the transverse position.
 The transverse offset is factory-set or set by the Bizerba service and
 may not be changed.
The motorized transverse adjustment for labelers is available and activated.
Mode level: 5
Modify transverse offset for current labeling job
 <Automat> / <Labeler> / <CrosswOffs. labeler>
 To reduce the transverse offset, enter the minus sign.
 Enter and confirm transverse offset in mm.
The labeler is automatically moved. The setting is not applied to the database.

title: Enter the maximum package height
text:
If the device is equipped with a motorized height adjustment for labelers, the different
 package heights can be saved in the automatic labeler parameter tables. When calling up
 an article that an automatic labeler parameter table is assigned to, the labeler is automati-
 cally adjusted to the respective package height. The labeler height can also be adjusted
 automatically using the softkeys or the keys located on the labeler.
 The motorized height adjustment for labelers is available and activated.
 Mode level: 1
 Modify package height for current labeling job
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Labeler man. offset>
 Enter value and confirm.
 The labeler is automatically adjusted to the relevant package height. The setting is not ap-
 plied to the database.

title: Adjusting labeler height by means of softkeys
text:
If the device is equipped with a motorized height adjustment for the labeler, the labeler
 height can be automatically adjusted using the softkeys. The labeler height can also be ad-
 justed automatically using the keys located on the labeler. If package height is saved un-
 der the automatic labeler parameters, the labeler height is changed in the event of a PLU
 change.
 During height adjustment of the labeler, there must not be any pack-
 ages under the labeler.
 The following functions are available:
 <Labeler UP>: Start height adjustment upwards.
 <Labeler DOWN> Start height adjustment downwards.
 <Labeler STOP> Stop height adjustment.
 After stopping the motorized height adjustment via the softkeys, the set height is displayed
 in the <Max. pckg. height> softkey.
 The motorized height adjustment for labelers is available and activated.

title: Mode level: 1
text: <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Labeler man. offset>

title: Enter transverse position of labeler
text:
If the device is equipped with a motorized transverse adjustment for labelers, the labeler
can automatically be moved to the desired position when the article is changed. To do so,
save the transverse position in the automatic labeler parameter table associated to the ar-
ticle, see page 250. For the current labeling job, you may directly enter or change the
transverse position of the labeler.
The motorized transverse adjustment for labelers is available and activated.
Mode level: 1
Modify the labeler's transverse position for the current labeling job
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Cross posit. labeler>
 Enter value and confirm.
The labeler is adjusted in transverse direction to transport direction. The setting is not ap-
plied to the database.

title: Adjusting the transverse position of the labeler via softkeys
text:
If the device is equipped with a motorized transverse adjustment for the labeler, the labeler
can be moved in transversal direction by means of softkeys. The transverse position can
also be adjusted automatically using the keys located on the labeler. If the transverse posi-
tion is saved under the automatic labeler parameters, it is changed according to these pa-
rameters in the event of a PLU change.
The following functions are available:
<Labeler FOWARD>: Start transverse adjustment forwards.
<Labeler BACKWARD> Start transverse adjustment backwards.
<Labeler STOP> Stop transverse adjustment.
After stopping the motorized transverse adjustment via the softkeys, the set transverse po-
sition is displayed in the <Cross posit. labeler> softkey.
The motorized transverse adjustment for labelers is available and activated.

title: Entering the label distance
text:
The label distance is the distance between the label stop edge at the printer mechanism
 and the reference line of the package. Depending on the setting, the reference line is the
 leading edge, trailing edge, or centerline of the package, see page 257. Which edge is
 considered the leading edge and which one the trailing edge depends on the transport di-
 rection of the package. The illustration shows how dimensioning of the label distance de-
 pends on the defined reference line and the transport direction of the package.
 Illustration 57: Label distance depending on reference line and transport direction
 1 Transport direction

title: Trailing edge of the package
text:
A: label distance when the leading edge of the package is the reference line.
 B: label distance when the center line of the package is the reference line.
 C: label distance when the trailing edge of the package is the reference line.
 You may enter the label distance in the automatic labeler parameters, see page 250. You
 may temporarily modify the label distance for the current labeling job.
 Mode level: 1
 Modify label distance for current labeling job
20 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Label distance>
 Enter and confirm value in mm.

title: Enter reference line for label distance
text:
By default, the leading edge of the package is defined as the reference line for label dis-
tance input. In this regard, leading edge and trailing edge refer to the transport direction of
the package.
You may enter another reference line in the automatic labeler parameters, see page 250.
You may temporarily change the reference line for the current labeling job.
 After changing the reference line, the label distance has to be adapted
 accordingly, see page 256. Determine the necessary distance by run-
 ning a labeling test.
The following settings are possible:
<Pckg. edge front side>: Reference line is the leading edge of the package. Default set-
 ting.
<Pckg. edge back side>: Reference line is the trailing edge of the package.
<Pckg. edge middle>: Reference line is the center line of the package.
Mode level: 1
Modify reference line for current labeling job
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Ref. point lab. distan.>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Piston labeler
text:
If the device is equipped with a piston labeler (labeling type: <Quick piston lab.>), labeling
can be adapted to the respective package or label using the parameters specified below.

title: Entering package height
text:
By defining the package height, the piston is started in such a manner as to ensure that
 the label is always applied to the same position on the package. If the database is config-
 ured accordingly, you may save the package height in the article data and in the automatic
 labeler data. You may temporarily change the package height for the current labeling job.
 If required, modifications can be saved to the database.
 Labeler type: <Quick piston lab.>
 Mode level: 1
 Enter the package height for the current labeling job
 <Device menu> / <Etc> / <Height of package>
 Enter value.
 To save the value to the database, activate the "->Database [Etc]" field.
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 Press <OK>.
 To save to the database, enter and confirm a password for mode level 3 (local) or
 4 (global).

title: Entering gripper offset
text:
After printing, the label is held by the vacuum nozzles of the gripper and transported under
 the labeling piston. If a label is not transported correctly, you can change the position of
 the gripper when it takes hold of the label. A positive value moves the gripper towards the
 piston.
 Labeler type: <Quick piston lab.>
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Etc> / <Quick piston lab.> / <Pickup mec. offset>
 Enter the minus sign for negative values.
 Enter value and confirm.
20

title: Entering rotational angle
text:
The piston of the piston labeler can be rotated degree by degree up to +/- 360 degrees. In
this manner the label can be applied to the package at any rotated position. The rotational
angle that is called up together with the article data, may be changed for the current label-
ing job. The modification can be saved to the database, if required.
Positive value: Label rotation in a counterclockwise direction
Negative value: Label rotation in a clockwise direction
Labeler type: <Quick piston lab.>
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Etc> / <Quick piston lab.> / <Angle of rotation>
 Enter value.
 To save the value to the database, activate the "->Database [Etc]" field.
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 Press <OK>.
 To save to the database, enter and confirm a password for mode level 3 (local) or
 4 (global).

title: Entering acceleration time
text:
During the predefined acceleration time, the piston is accelerated downwards. By chang-
ing the acceleration period, the impact force is set.
Labeler type: <Quick piston lab.>
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Etc> / <Quick piston lab.> / <Accelerat. time>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Entering extension time
text:
During the predefined extension time, the piston moves at almost constant speed. Once
this time elapsed, the piston returns to the basic position. When the labeling performance
worsens considerably, "smooth" labeling can be set by increasing the acceleration time
and decreasing the extension time.
Labeler type: <Quick piston lab.>
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Etc> / <Quick piston lab.> / <Extending time>
 Enter value and confirm.

title: Rotary arm labeler
text:
If the device is equipped with a rotary arm labeler (labeling type: <Rotary arm labeler>),
labeling can be adapted to the respective package or label using the parameters specified
below.
 The preset parameters may only be changed after consultation with Bi-
 zerba service.

title: Rotation parameter
text:
The rotary arm labeler parameters are set prior to delivery. If settings have to be custom-
 ized, the values can be adapted accordingly. After changing parameters, adjustment of
 other rotation parameters may be required. See the service manual for detailed informa-
 tion on the rotary arm labeler and relative settings.

title: Belt labeler
text:
The belt labeler is a labeling system for bottom labeling. If the device is equipped with a
 belt labeler (labeling type: <Belt labeler>), labeling can be adapted to the respective pack-
 age or label using the parameters specified below.

Here you may enter an additional delay time for a stand-alone labeler that is activated by

Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Labeler> / <Etc> / <Delay>

title: Switching on or off the auxiliary belts
text:
Under certain circumstances, packages of critical dimensions must be laterally guided dur-
ing transport to avoid toppling over. For this reason, auxiliary belts can be mounted on the
transport belts. This function allows switching on and off the auxiliary belts. The following
settings are possible:
"On": Auxiliary belts switched off. Standard setting.
"Off": Auxiliary belts switched on.
The conveyor belts are equipped with auxiliary belts which are activated.
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Transport equipment> / <Supplement. belts>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Registration of light barrier masking section
text:
Packages with an irregular external form may trigger a light barrier several times. In order
 to avoid this, define a masking section. After the first edge of the package, the light barrier
 is deactivated for the length of the masking section. You may set different masking sec-
 tions for light barrier 1 and further light barriers 2 and 3.
 First work with the shortest masking section. Only use a higher value if your packages re-
 quire it, for example foil packages or packages with holes. The masking section of each
 article should be smaller than the package length as the back edge of the package is not
 recognized.
 If the masking section is too long, this impairs package detection and
 may stop processing.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <LB1 susp. path>
 Register masking section for light barrier 1 and confirm.
 <Device menu> / <LB2/3 susp. path>
 Register masking section for further light barriers and confirm.

title: Selecting transmitting current of light barrier
text:
If the light barrier does not detect critical packages properly, e.g. reflecting packages, you
 can select a higher transmission current for the light barrier. The following settings are
 possible:
 – <20 mA>
 – <40 mA>
 – <60 mA>
 – <80 mA>
 Mode level: 5
 <Automat> / <Light barriers> / <Send current>
 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Entering belt speed for labeling
text:
The belt speed determines the system throughput. Choose belt speed to prevent package
jam in front of the device. The following cases might require a reduction in belt speed:
– long packages
– heavy packages
– small support surface
– large labels
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Transport equipment> / <Speed>

text:
You may change the speed of the conveyor belt within the values valid for the device. Se-
lect the belt speed matching to the speed of the on-site conveying direction.

text:
The device sorts packages via varying separation belt speeds and also via an upstream-
integrated infeed belt (optional). The separation factor is the relation of these belts.
Mode level: 1

 Enter and confirm separation factor.

and outputs. The following settings are possible:

"–": Negative logic. A signal change of +24 V to 0 V is an active sig-

dividers:

title: Configure synchronization message of weighing belt
text:
In order to synchronize package processing, the weighing belt sends a synchronization
 message, which has to be canceled by one of the following events to allow a package
 through:
 – by a PLU change
 – by a GxNet interface command
 A synchronization message that is not canceled has a different impact, depending on the
 operating mode set for the weighing belt:
 With The package stops on the scales until the synchronization mes-
 <Weighing Start/Stop>: sage has been cleared.
21
 With If the package has reached the end of the weighing belt and the
 <Weighing Continuous>: synchronization message has not yet been cleared, the pack-
 age is treated as if defective and might be rejected.
With this function, you determine how the synchronization message can be canceled. The
following settings are possible:
"no": No synchronization. Default setting.
"Release by entering The synchronization message is canceled by a PLU change or
PLU": by a GxNet interface command.
"Release only by enter- The synchronization message can only be canceled with a
ing command": GxNet interface command.

<Fixed value>: Label packages with pre-defined price and weight.

title: Enter total tare for totals 1 to 3
text:
It might be necessary to add the empty weight of the box, container or pallet to the calcula-
 ted tare totals of the individual packages in totals 1 to 3.
 The following rules apply when forming totals:
 Tare total *1:
 – The tare total for total 1 is increased for each package by the tare weight of the pack-
 age.
 – If printing total 1 or if the preset value for total 1 is reached, a prespecified total1 tare
 is added to the tare total for total 1. Total1-tare, for example, corresponds to the box
 weight.

title: Tare total *1 = (total of single tare) + (total1-tare)
text:
Tare total *2: Total 2 counts single packages
– The tare total for total 2 is increased for each package by the tare weight of the pack-
 age.
– If printing total 2 or if the preset value for total 2 is reached, a prespecified total2 tare
 is added to the tare total for total 2. Total2-tare, for example, corresponds to the box
 weight.
Tare total *2 = (total of single tare) + (total2-tare)
Tare total *2: Total 2 counts to trigger total 1
– The tare total for total 2 is increased for each package by the tare weight of the pack-
 age.
– When printing total 1 or when the preselection for total 1 is reached, total1-tare is add-
 ed to the tare total for total 2. Total1-tare, for example, corresponds to the box weight.
– When printing total 2 or when the preselection for total 2 is reached, total2-tare is add-
 ed to the tare totalfor total 2. Total2-tare corresponds to the pallet weight for example.
When total 1 is triggered x n, the tare total *2 is established as follows:
Tare total *2 = (total of single tare) +n(Total1+tare) + (Total2-tare)

title: Set up total release
text:
This is where you can define how a total is printed once the related total preselection has
been reached. The settings only takes effect when a total preselection is set for the re-
spective total. The following types of total releases are supported:
by hand: The total label is triggered manually via a softkey once the total
 is reached.
synchronous: The total label is automatically printed once the total is reached.
 When the last package that belongs to the total has left the con-
 veyor belts, they stop during total stop and the total label is prin-
 ted automatically.
 Once a total has been triggered it is no longer possible to cancel the in-
 cluded packages.
 In the totals stop a new total preselection or PLU change can
 be executed. After accepting and confirming the totals label the
 package that had been stopped on the scales, is weighed. The
 conveyor belts continue. Between the last package containing
 one triggered total and the first package of the new total is a
 gap.
 This selection enables total switches or package ejectors to be
 controlled.
asynchronous: The total label is printed automatically by an external printer
 when the total is reached. No total stop takes place.
 The package is not totalized until it has left the automatic ma-
 chine. That is why no cancellations are required if errors occur.
 Up to three total print jobs can be sent to an external pr

text:

title: Use total preselection column
text:
With the totalization type <PLU dynamic>, you can label up to 40 nested articles at the

 tion column. The rows correspond to those in the total preselection matrix, see page 299.

title: Total evaluation
text:
As well as the general and PLU or weight class-specific total memories (total preselection

 – Weight total
 – Gross weight total
 – Tare total

 ted database table is set to "local" (standard setting). The database ta-
 bles CONFSUM1, CONFSUM2 and CONFSUM3 are not defined for the

 The configuration of the database is not subject of this documentation.
 For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizer-
 ba Service.

title: Weight classes
text:
Weight-class-specific labeling enables the following functions:
 – Label packages dependent on their weight differently.
 – In labelers with an integrated package separator or divider: Automatically separate
 overweight or underweight packages.
 – For packages in a specific weight class print an alternative label on another labeler,
 e.g. double labeler.
 – Check that fixed weight packages comply with the statutory stipulated tolerance range
 and create corresponding statistics.
 Use the weight class tables as a basis for weight-class-specific labeling. For each weight
 class, enter the nominal weights, types of statistics, upper or lower tolerance limits, prices,
 texts, codes, etc. in the columns of the weight class table, see page 313.
 You can create different weight class tables and save them under weight class numbers in
 the database. You can use the weight class number to allocate a weight class table to a
 PLU, with the result that it can be accessed automatically when the PLU is changed.
 To facilitate the handling of weight class tables, there are input tools available for each sta-
 tistic type, that only request the data relevant to the specific statistic type and transfer them
 automatically to the current weight class table, see page 320.
 You can modify the weight class data for the current labeling job, see page 319.
 You need the license "Prepack Regulation li

title: Conditions for package infeed
text:
Adjust package infeed to avoid package jam on the automatic labeler belts.
In automatic weighing instruments, a zero point adjustment of the scales is required after a
specific period of time or number of packages. For this reason, labeling is interrupted for a
short time. Make sure that there will not be any package jam not even in this case.
Singling packages automatically
If packages are fed at irregular intervals, they can be automatically pre-singled between
feed belt and singling belt and completely singled between singling belt and weighing belt.
For this, adjust the speed ratio between the feed belt and the singling belt so that the sin-
gling belt stops only for a very short time when packages approach the feed belt one after
the other at very short distance, see page 263.
Observing the minimum distance between packages
If packages are manually fed, the weighing belt length is considered the minimum distance
between the packages to be kept.
The package distance is the distance between two similar package edges, e.g. between
the leading edge of package 1 and the leading edge of package 2.
Choosing the correct labeling belt speed
The belt speed depends on the label printing time and label size. If belt speed is too high,
the "Label too slow" message is displayed. Reduce belt speed in this case, see page 263.

classes are corrected.

an error message appears.

title: Setting operating mode in case of error
text:
The device counts faulty packages in succession. The causes of the error could be:
 – Package separation error
 – Scales not at rest
 – Minimum weight error
 Determine here how the device should react when a prespecified number of faulty pack-
 ages is reached. The following settings are possible:
 "Stop" The device stops at the prespecified number of successive faul-
 ty packages.
 "Conv." At the prespecified number of successive faulty packages, the
 device switches to transport operation.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Error handling> / <Automat on error>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Set error number for automatic stop
text:
With the following functions you can set the number of errors separately for general pack-
 age errors and transmission errors after which the device should stop, or switch to trans-
 port operation, see page 356.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Error handling> / <Acc. to frequency>
 Press <Stop after errors>.
 Enter and confirm the number for general errors.
 Press <Stop after send error>.
 Enter and confirm the number of transmission errors.

title: Set the approval rights for remote-controlled lock status
text:
A higher-ranking EDP system provides a special command (XCW_LOCK) which you can
 use to stop processing (LOCK). Use this function to determine who this special lock status
 can be reverted again. The following settings are possible:
 <Dialog or The release is possible on the device or via the interface on.
 XCW_LOCK>:
 <Only XCW_UNLOCK>: The release is only possible on the device.
 <Only via dialog>: The release is only possible via the interface.
 Mode level: 5
 <Main menu> / <Processing> / <Release XCW_LOCK>
25 Press softkey with respective setting.

title: Service print-outs
text:
You can print different service printouts. Depending on how the device is configured, it
sends data to a printer, for example, or to a storage medium or connected computer.

title: Select device for service printouts
text:
If the device is integrated in a system network, you can trigger service printouts from all
devices in the system network. Select the devices here from which you want to trigger
service printouts.
In the device selection table you have 4 rows in which to select up to 32 devices based on
the respective device ID. You can only select devices that are included in the system net-
work. The fields of the device IDs that are not used in the system network, cannot be acti-
vated.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Device selection>
 The following preselections are supported:
 "only own" In the following table for device selection only your own de-
 vice has been selected.
 "all" In the following table for device selection all devices from
 the system network have been selected.
 "no" In the following table for device selection, no device has
 been selected.
 Make a preselection and press <OK>.
 The table appears for you to select a device.
 Select or deselect devices by tapping the respective fields.
 Close table.
 To save setting reply to security query with <yes>.

title: Setting smaller character set for service printouts
text:
Ticket rolls at least 68 mm in width are required for service printouts and printouts of table
editors with the standard character set. If only ticket rolls with a width of 58 mm are availa-
ble, you can define a smaller character set here. Printouts can be made at a reduced size
on 58 mm wide ticket rolls as well.
Possible settings:
"Std.": Standard character height for 68 mm labels.
"LC": Smaller character height for 58 mm labels.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> / <Chara. set serv.print.>
 Select setting and confirm.

title: Redirecting service printouts
text:
You can redirect service printouts to the following targets:
 "Label printer": The device sends print jobs to the label printer. Default setting.
 "List print. interface": The device sends printouts to the configured list printer.
 "Only e-service": The device only sends printouts to eService. If this setting is ac-
 tive, the device does not print out any more statistic reports al-
 so.
 Mode level: 2
 <Printer + interface> / <List printer> / <Deviating print service print>
 Press softkey with respective setting.
 The setting is active.

title: Printing device settings
text:
This function enables you to print selected device settings. From the selection table you
 can choose the following device settings for printing:
 "Outgoing lines": This includes the connection parameters, "PSV_PCK WDout
 flag", "Add.data to PSV_PCK", "Contents of PSV_DATA",
 "Send if data is mod.", "Add. data to statistics".
 "EDP interface": This contains the AEDP parameters, Gx-Com parameters, list
 printer parameters, scanner parameters.
 "Conf. data Delta prin.": Modified default settings (Delta configuration).
 "Configuration": This contains the scales configuration and total configuration.
 "Configuration (tables)": This includes the Ethernet address, weight class data, totals
 preselection data.
 "DB attribute config.": The database attribute configuration contains GGDAT, GGETI-
 KET, AMPAR, GGCAB, GGSUM, GGSCAN.
 "Menu tree Mode T": Menu tree for mode level T.
 "Connecting multi-label- This includes printer channel control for multiple labelers.
 er":
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> / <Print device set.>
 The selection table appears showing the device settings you could print.
 Select the device settings you want to print and close the table.
 To start the service printout, reply to the security question with <yes>.
 The device sends data to the printer that has been configured.
25

title: Print log book of metal detector
text:
Only for devices with a metal detector. The protocols in this logbook document the com-
plete production process. The documentation guidelines set by HACCP regulations are ful-
filled.
The following print functions are available:
"Archive protocol": The protocol contains the following information including date
 and time. Information is listed chronologically in the protocol.
 The device deletes all information once it has been completely
 printed without any errors:
 – Metal detection
 – Errors and operational interruptions that have occurred
 – Product change
 – Changes to the device setting togs
 – Start, end and progression of the test routines
"Temporary protocol": Same content as "Archive protocol". The device does not de-
 lete information after it has been completely printed out without
 any errors.
"Product statistics": Statistics contain the following information:
 – Begin and end of inspection of a specific product
 – Device settings
 – Statistical data about the number of products, metal detec-
 tion and errors
"Charge statistics": Same content as "Product statistics". Use this statistics if you
 produce the same product for different brands or chain of
 stores.
"Data on device": The printout contains information on the device and its settings:
 – Production line, device identification, date, time
 – Software status, search frequency, conveyor speed
 – activated/dea

title: Diagnostic tool
text:
The diagnoses lists are used by Bizerba Service.
 For additional information, please contact Bizerba Service.
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> / <Diagnostics tool>
 Select and confirm function.
 The device sends the data to the configured printer, or deletes the data if the delete func-
 tion has been selected.

title: Print internal device status
text:
This function enables you to print multiple lists and the history of reports to be analyzed
 internally by Bizerba Service, see page 129.
 For additional information, please contact Bizerba Service.
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> / <Print int. dev. state>
 Select and confirm list.
 The device sends data to the printer that has been configured.
25

title: Print menu tree and set parameters
text:
This function enables you to print the following information:
– "Compl. menu tree (w/o free softkeys)"
– "Compl. menu tree (with free softkeys)"
– "Softkeys copied from Mode T"
– "Value range of all options"
– "Ethernet address"
 For additional information, please contact Bizerba Service.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> /
 <Menu tree/ Fix. param.>
 Select and confirm list.
The device sends data to the printer that has been configured.

title: Printing resource data
text:
With this function you can print the layout and field contents of all the customer labels
saved in the device.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Service printouts> / <Etc> /
 <Print re- source data>
 Confirm selection "Layout and field contents of all cust. labels".
The device sends data to the printer that has been configured.

title: Testing belt tension of conveyor belts
text:
During the test the display shows the transmitter signals.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <Automat> / <Test belt tension>
Depending on the previous status, the test either starts or stops the conveyor belts.

title: Testing belt drives
text:
Functions to test the following belt drives are available:
 <Test IC>: Starts the feed belt for 2 seconds.
 <Test SC>: Starts the separation belt for 2 seconds.
 <Test WC>: Starts the weighing belt for 2 seconds.
 <Test LC 1> to Starts the respective labeling belt for 2 seconds.
 <Test LC 4>:
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <Automat> / <Test belt drive>
 Press the required softkey.
 The conveyor belt starts immediately and stops after 2 seconds.

title: Test printer
text:
The following functions are available to test the label printer:
 <Printer ONLINE>: Deletes the working memory for label printing. The next single
 label is prepared completely from scratch.
 <Printer OFFLINE>: Activates printing of a test label, as follows:
 – activate once: normal test picture
 – activate twice: smaller test picture
 Start printing with <Start printing> softkey.
 <Start printing>: Starts printing a test label.
 <Printer status>: Indicates status of printer. Possible settings:
 – "Std.": no status display. Standard setting.
 – "Bin.": Status display.
 The following printer stati are displayed:
 – "Idle": Printer task is waiting for jobs.
 – "Print": Print job is running.
 – "PQuick": Print job is running.
 – "WBer.": Printer task is waiting until tear-off light barrier is
 free again.
 – "Feed": Empty feed cycle is running.
 – "InitC": Cold start initialization for printer task is running.
 – "Prep.": Preparatory calculation for label is running.
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <Printer>
 Press softkey with respective Function.
25

title: Test scales
text:
You can activate a variety of scale test modes in order to test the scales.
 For further information please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizer-
 ba Service.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <Automat> / <Developer param. scale>
 Enter and confirm the number of the scale test mode.

title: Check if within permissible verification limits
text:
This function tests the verification error limits.
 This test is usually performed by Bizerba Service. For further informa-
 tion please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <Automat> / <Verifiy article>
 Perform the test procedure in accordance with the instructions on the screen.

title: Delete remote soft keys
text:
A higher-ranking EDP system can assign the softkey of the device for its own purposes. If
a softkey is pressed, in this case, the result goes directly to the EDP system. In the event
of a fault, it might be necessary to delete the softkeys assigned to the EDP system and to
switch off the online connection. Afterwards, the device can be operated directly again.
 When data are transmitted to the EDP system and the connection is in-
 terrupted, you have to deselect the affected EDP channel in order to
 continue processing, see page 419.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Etc> / <Del. remote softkeys>

title: Manage licenses
text:
You can acquire additional software licenses for the device. Ex works each device is given
 trial licenses relating to a date and operating time.
 The following functions are available:
 – Enter license code to activate licenses, see page 364
 – Print list of licenses, see page 364
 – Switch on or off demo or test licenses, see page 364
 – Switch licenses on or off, see page 365

title: Activate licenses
text:
If you acquire licensable software retrospectively, you receive a license code. With this li-
 cense code you can activate the license for your device.
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Licences>
 The list of available functions appears. "Enter licence code" is highlighted.
 Press <ok>.
 A table is shown. If several devices exist, the table contains a row for each device.
 In the column "Licence code" enter the license code for the desired device.
 Close table.
 If the license code is valid, the software license is activated.

title: Print a list of licenses
text:
In order to obtain an overview of all activated licenses, you can print a complete list.
 Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Licences>
 The list of available functions appears.
 Select "Print licence list" and press <ok>.
 The device sends data to the printer that has been configured. Activated licenses are
 marked in the list with "[+]". Non-activated licenses are marked in the list with "[-]".

title: Switch on/off the demo and trial licenses
text:
You can switch off any demo or trial licenses. This allows you to check if all the functions
 you required are supported without the demo and trial licenses. If the functions you require
 are not supported, you must configure your device differently, or acquire the missing licen-
 ses.
26
The following licenses permit the following:
Demo license: Authorization of licensable software a specific, date-relevant
 pre-specified period.
Trial license. The licensable software available for you to use for a prespeci-
 fied period without charge. The remaining time is displayed next
 to the license icon in the lower part of the display in
 hours: . A trial license switches off automatically when
 the remaining time is less than 100 hours. You can switch the
 trial license back on again and use it until the time period has
 expired. In the meantime, procure the required licenses.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Licences>
 The list of available functions appears.
 Select "Activate demo/test license" or "Demo/test licence OFF" and press <ok>.

title: Switch licenses on and off
text:
You can switch off the licenses. Softkeys of licensable functions are displayed in gray and
access is locked. The icon appears on the display.
Mode level: 5
 <Service menu> / <System services> / <Licences>
 The list of available functions appears.
 Select "Licences on" or "Licences off" and press <ok>.
27

title: Formatting storage medium
text:
A new storage medium should be formatted before starting the first data backup.
 CAUTION During formatting all data on the storage medium are to be de-
 leted!
 Possible data loss.
 – Before starting formatting, check if there are data on the storage
 medium and if these data are still needed.
 Mode level: 5
 Storage medium in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Format storage medium>
 To format the storage medium reply to security query with <yes>.

title: Saving line backup
text:
In the case of a line with several devices you can save the data from all devices in one
work step. The system bus address of the devices may not be subsequently modified.
 Macros saved with the display and operating unit GT-12 C, the GT-12 C
 saves and not the device. Therefore these macros are missing in a line
 back-up of the device.
Requirements:
– The devices that belong to the line are defined, see page 371.
– The devices are connected with each other via the system bus.
– The devices are switched on.
– Mode level: 5
 Make sure that the storage medium is inserted in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Line backup> / <Store line>
 Enter the name of the data backup. Comply with the rules for DOS file names.
 Press <ok>.
 A table occurs. The table columns contain the devices that belong to the line. The ta-
 ble rows contain different data groups. You can select the device from which you want
 to save data. Non-existing data groups cannot be selected.
Select data
 Select or deselect a data group for each device: Touch the table field until the re-
 quired setting occurs.
or
 Select all data groups for a device: Select the table head of the device. Press <Set>
 in the following inquiry.
or
 Deselect all data groups for a device: Select the table head of the device. Press
 <Delete> in the following inquiry.
or
 Select a data group for all devices: Select the data group in the left ta

text:
Only load a line backup back to the line where it has come from.
Requirements:
– The devices are connected with each other via the system bus.
– The devices are switched on.
– Automatic processing has stopped.
– Mode level: 5
 Make sure that the storage medium is inserted in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Line backup> / <Load line>
 Select a line back-up and press <ok>.
 The following message appears: "When loading setups, the backup setup is auto-
 matically activated and the devices are switched off/on.".
 Press <ok>.
 The following question appears: "Adopt only local master data?".
Load local or all master data
 Only load local master data: Select "yes" and press <ok>. Continue with "Which attrib-
 ute configuration do you wish to use for database?".
or
 Load all master data: Select "no" and press <ok>.
Re-create master data or add
 Re-create master data, overwrite master data on device: Select "Create" and press

or
