"Which attribute configuration do you wish to use for database?"
 Load attribute configurati

title: Display status of line backup
text:
During a line backup you can have the progress of data transmission displayed. The data
 from each device is completely transferred before line backup of the next device begins.
 The table contains information on each device and data group as to whether the data has
 already been transferred or not. The table has the following icons:
 "OK": Date completely transmitted.
 "X": Data is being transferred.
 "---": Data are not being transferred.
 Display of a number: An error has occurred. Tip the number. You will receive a plain
 text message of the error.
 Mode level: 5
 <Storage medium> / <Line backup> / <Line state>
 The status of the line back-up is displayed.

title: Delete line backup
text:
Delete the line backups you no longer required.
 Mode level: 5
 Make sure that the storage medium is inserted in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Line backup> / <Cancel line>
 Select the line backup to be deleted.
 CAUTION The device deletes the line backup immediately after it has
 been exported!
 Data loss during faulty selection.
 – Select line backup carefully.
 Press <OK>.
 The line backup has been deleted.

title: Select device for line backup
text:
If a line comprises several devices, you can determine here which devices shall be inclu-
ded in the line backup. This selection applies to the line backup of devices and for the
loading of the line backup onto the devices.
In 4 lines in the table you can select up to 32 devices with the respective device ID. You
can only select devices that are included in the system network. The fields of the device
IDs that are not used in the system network, cannot be activated.
Illustration 66: Select device for line backup
Mode level: 5
 <Storage medium> / <Line backup> / <Line dev.select.>
 By touching the respective table fields devices are selected or deselected.
 Close table with < >.
 To save device selection reply to security query with <yes>.
27

title: Save user-defined softkeys
text:
User-defined softkeys can be created in mode level T, see page 121. These user-defined
 softkeys can be saved to a storage medium.
 Mode level: 5
 Make sure that the storage medium is inserted in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Userdef. softkeys> / <Sm:Store softkeys>
 Enter name of softkey backup. The name can be a maximum of four characters, e. g.
 SOF1. Take note of large and small case.
 Press <ok>.
 If no softkeys are saved on the storage medium under the same name, the user-de-
 fined softkeys are saved immediately.
 If the storage medium already includes a softkey backup with the same name, a se-
 curity query appears.
 Overwrite backup file. Select "yes" and press <ok>.

title: Load user-defined softkeys
text:
User-defined softkeys can be loaded from storage medium.
 Mode level: 5
 Make sure that the storage medium is inserted in device.
 <Storage medium> / <Userdef. softkeys> / <Sm:Load softkeys>
 Select softkey backup and confirm.
 The following message appears: "Data loaded".

title: Setup
text:
The set-up saves all the settings except for the database and the BOS archive (BOS:
 Basic Operation System). The device copies the data to a permanent memory area. The
 device can save a maximum of three setups. The setups can be additionally copied to a
 storage medium and loaded from a storage medium.

title: Save setup
text:
Mode level: 5
 <Setup> / <Create setup>
 Enter name of setup. The name can be a maximum of four characters, e. g. SET1.
 Take note of large and small case.
 Press <ok>.
 If no setup is saved under the same name and if there have not been saved three set-
 ups yet, the new setup is saved immediately.
 If a setup has already been saved with the same name, this message appears: "Set-
 up name existing.Select new name.".
 If three setups have already been saved, the following message appears: "No more
 free capacity for setup.". In order to save a new setup, an old setup needs to be de-
 leted, see page 374.
 If need be, confirm message with <ok>.
 The data are not saved.

title: Activate setup
text:
Stored setups can be activated at any time. Plan carefully with which setup you want to
change the data of the device.
The @INI setup contains the works settings of the device and is always included in a data
backup. The @SAV setup is produced during the first line backup. With each additional
line backup, @SAV is updated.
 An imported setup cannot be activated until the device has been switch-
 ed off and on again.
Mode level: 5
 <Setup> / <Activate setup>
 Select a setup and press <ok>.
 The following message appears: "Important data modification: Process can only be
 done after switch on/off of device.".
 Press <ok>.
 Switch device off and on.
The new setup is active after a restart.
27

title: Delete setup
text:
Delete setups you no longer require. This frees up storage space for new setups. The de-
 vice can save a maximum of 3 setups. Only the Bizerba customer services can delete the
 Service Setup @BIZ.
 CAUTION The device deletes the setup immediately after you have confirmed
 with <ok>!
 Possible data loss.
 – Select setup carefully.
 Mode level: 5
 <Setup> / <Clear setup>
 Select a setup and press <ok>.
 The setup is deleted immediately.

title: Remove storage medium safely
text:
Use this function before removing a storage medium from the device.
 CAUTION If removed without running function beforehand
 <Remove storage medium safely> data can be lost!
 – Before removing storage medium run function
 <Remove storage medium safely>.
 Mode level: 5
 <Storage medium> / <Remove storage medium safely>
 A message appears after a few seconds: "St. medium can be safely removed!".
 Remove storage medium.

title: General information
text:
Only if maintenance and service are run regularly the device and its functions are secure.
It is absolutely important that the maintenance cycles are maintained. The cleaning and
maintenance plans enable an overview of all cleaning measures and planable mainte-
nance activities.
If you have any questions or problems regarding cleaning and/or maintenance works,
please contact the Bizerba Service.

title: Safety measures
text:
The maintenance works require knowledge of machine and safety technology as well as
mechanics and/or electronics. Therefore, the maintenance works must only be run be au-
thorized personnel. This applies especially for all electronic works.
 When carrying out cleaning and maintenance works outside the switch
 cabinet, switch off maintenance switch and unplug mains switch. Switch
 of compressed air supply.
 DANGER Electrical voltage in the switch cabinet even when the main switch
 is switched off!
 Risk of death due to electrical shock.
 – Before carrying out work in the switch cabinet, disconnect the pow-
 er connector.
 – Work in the switch cabinet may only be carried out by qualified
 trade personnel or Bizerba service technicians.
 WARNING Compressed air supply remains on when device is switched off -
 also if power supply is disconnected!
 When working on the device risk of injury at compressed-air oper-
 ated device parts.
 – Switch of compressed air supply before start working on the de-
 vice.

title: CAUTION      Automatically starting components!
text:
During automatic operation components can switch on and off au-
 tomatically. Serious injuries and damage to property can result.
 – Wear closely fitting clothes and a hair-net.
 – Do not wear necklaces, ties etc.
 – Keep fingers and hands away from moving parts.
 – Switch off the device at the main switch before carrying out clean-
 ing and maintenance work.
 CAUTION Risk of entanglement by rotating parts!
 During automatic operation there is a risk of entanglement be-
 tween rotating device parts. Serious injuries and damage to prop-
 erty can result.
 – Wear closely fitting clothes and a hair-net.
 – Do not wear necklaces, ties etc.
 – Keep fingers and hands away from moving parts.
 CAUTION Damage to conveyor belts!
 Possible damage to property due to objects on conveyor belt.
 – Do not place any objects on conveyor belts. Do not use conveyor
 belts for storage.

Clean conveyor belts regularly with suitable cleaning agents as per cleaning and service

tions.

title: Display thermal strip type
text:
If the labeler is only used as a label dispenser and no printed is integra-
 ted, only the "Label dispenser" text is displayed.
 Mode level: 5

title: Activating or deactivating Smart Label (RFID labels)
text:
With this function you activate or deactivate processing of RFID labels, see page 234. The
 following settings are possible:
 "W/o": No processing of RFID labels. Default setting.
 "With": Processing of RFID Labels.
 Mode level: 5
 <Printer> / <Printer equipment> / <Smart Label>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Activate or deactivate reverse mode
text:
When using an EcoMotion printer, this function cannot be applied, as it
 isn't needed.
With this function, you can switch reverse mode for the current labeling job on or off. In
reverse mode, the label is retracted by about 10 mm in order to be printed from the begin-
ning again. This is required in the following cases:
– in Linerless labels
– to print variable data on the first 10 mm of a label
– to print the first 10 mm of a label that is rotated by 180 degrees on the label roll
The following settings are possible:
"W/o": Reverse mode is switched off. Standard setting.
"With": Reverse mode is switched on.
You usually enter this setting in the label parameter table, see page 201. When a PLU is
changed reverse mode is automatically switched on or off depending on the setting in the
label parameter table.
Mode level: 1 or 2
Switch on/off reverse mode for the current labeling job
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Retract operation>
or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Retract operation>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Choose thermal direct printing or thermal transfer printing
text:
If the device is equipped with a thermal transfer printing extension, you can choose be-
tween thermal direct and thermal transfer operating modes. The following settings are pos-
sible:
"Dir.": Thermal direct printing for thermal labelers. Standard setting.
"Trsf.": Thermal transfer printing when you are using thermal transfer
 film.
Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Print mode: thermal...>
or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Print mode: thermal...>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Sent print output
text:
With this function you determine which material is printed on. The following settings are
29 possible:
 "Lab.w. backing paper": Print feed is controlled by the gap between the labels or by the
 black synchronization strips on the backing tape.
 "Lab. w/o back. paper": E.g. for flag labels. The part that should not be printed is moved
 over quickly.
 "Ticket w/o preprHead": For ticket rolls (strip-printing operations).
 "Ticket w.preprHeader": The ticket paper is treated like a label, i.e. a successive header
 is printed.
 Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Etc> / <Print out- put to ...>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Etc> / <Print out- put to ...>
 Select setting and confirm.

title: Modify label feed
text:
If a label is dispensed too early or too late from the backing tape, enter either a larger or
 smaller value as label feed. You can modify the label feed with positive or negative values
 in both directions. The label feed unit is the dot. How the feed value correlates to a single
 dot depends on the printing head you are using.
 Example: Printing head with 8 dot/mm⇒ 1 dot corresponds to 1 mm / 8 = 0.125 mm.
 Label feed is usually entered in the label parameter table, see page 201. When a PLU is
 called up, the label feed in the related label parameter table is set automatically.
 With this function you can enter or change the label feed for the current labeling job.
 Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Label feed>
 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Label feed>
 For smaller label feeds, enter a minus sign.
 Enter value and confirm input.

title: Change horizontal and vertical print position
text:
If the text is printed adjusted in a horizontal or vertical direction, you can correct this by
entering a dot value. Usually the adjustment value is entered specific to each label in the
label parameter table, see page 201. With this function you can enter or change the ad-
justment value for the current labeling job.
Positive and negative adjustment values have the following impact:
Vertical print position
– Move in printing direction: Enter positive value.
– Move against printing direction: Enter negative value.
Horizontal print position
– Move to the left: Enter positive value.
– Move to the right: Enter negative value.
The procedure is described for mode level 2. In mode level 1 you have to press <Etc> first.
The continued procedure is the same as in mode level 2.
Mode level: 1 or 2
 <Labels> / <Printer menu>
 Press <Hor. print position>.
or
 Press <Vert. print position>.
 Enter and confirm adjustment in dot.

title: Select position on rip-off edge
text:
The back corner and front corner can be selected as the pull-off edge position.
Setting "LE": The back edge of the printed label is positioned with reference
 to the tear-off edge. Standard setting.
Setting "TE": The front edge of the next label is positioned at the tear-off
 edge.
Mode level: 1 or 2
 Mode level 1: <Etc> / <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Position tearoffEdge>
or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Etc> / <Position tearoffEdge>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Modify printing speed
text:
29
 If the print quality in labels that are not very good is insufficient, enter a lower printing

 that is used. This is checked when entries are made.
 You usually enter the printing speed in the label parameter table, see page 201. When a
 PLU is called up, the printing speed is set automatically from the related label parameter
 table. With this function you can change the printing speed for the current labeling job.

 or
 Mode level 2: <Labels> / <Printer menu> / <Print speed>
 Enter value and confirm input.

text:
For example, at very low temperatures, you can adjust the density and influence the quali-
 ty of printing. You can effect a change by specifying a positive or negative percentage val-
 ue. The range of values depends on the integrated dot bar.

 or

If the label is not printed evenly across the whole width, it can be corrected by turning the

title: Calibrating label light barrier
text:
You can calibrate the label light barrier at the printhead automatically.
Mode level: 5
 <Printer> / <Light barriers> / <Auto. calib. LB send.cur.>
 The following message appears: "Insert backing paper in printer leave printer open."
 Open printhead and insert backing paper without labels.
 Press <OK>.
 The label light barriers will be calibrated. After calibration the following message ap-
 pears: "LB adjustmentterminated, insert paper."
 Insert paper.
 Close printing mechanism and device.

title: Select label light barrier
text:
Devices with EcoMotion printers have two label light barriers; only one of them at a time is
29 active. In the event of unsuitable label lengths, the gap between two labels when in the
 stop position can be precisely when it's in the active light barrier. This causes problems
 detecting the front edge of the next label. In this case, switch to the other label light barrier.
 The following settings are possible:
 "Automatic": Automatic activation of the label light barrier that is furthest
 away from the label gap when in stop position.
 "Labels-LS1": Activate light barrier 1. Standard setting.
 "Labels-LS1": Activate light barrier 2.
 Only for devices with EcoMotion printing mechanisms.
 Mode level: 5
 <Printer> / <Light barriers> / <Labels- LB selectio>
 Select setting and confirm.

title: Modify the transmission current of the label light barriers
text:
The transmission current from the label light barriers is calculated during the automatic cal-
 ibration process and, if necessary, can be changed here by Bizerba Service. Example: La-

 Mode level: 5
 <Printer> / <Light barriers> / <Send.current offs.lab.LB1>
 Enter and confirm the percentage value.

title: Set label contrast
text:
If the label is not precisely positioned for printing, label contrast can be increased. In this
 way, the label edge is more easily detected and the label can be positioned more precisely
 in the printer. The following settings are possible:
 "Low" Low label contrast. Standard setting.
 "High" High label contrast. Set if the label edge is not correctly detec-
 ted.
 Mode level: 5
 <Printer> / <Light barriers> / <Labels- contrast>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Enter diameter of the label roll for supply message
text:
You can enter the minimum outer diameter of the label roll in order to monitor how many
labels you still have. When the preset external diameter has been reached, the warning
signal appears "Paper supply?". A signal can also be issued via a warning lamp, see
page 269.
Mode level: 5

title: Interface overview
text:
The device is equipped with the following interfaces:
30

 – Serial Interfaces, see page 400

 Via these interfaces you can transmit or receive data and commands to and from other de-
 vices.

title: Output port
text:
The output to the I/O port is used to control external devices such as transportation sys-
 tems or packaging machines.
 The output port is set up by Bizerba Service. For further information
 please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service.

title: Systembus
text:
The systembus connects devices in a system network. It operates via profibus or Ethernet.
 Each connected device has a unique systembus address.
30 The systembus is set up by Bizerba Service. For further information
 please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service.

title: TCP/IP (Ethernet)
text:
Your device is fitted with an Ethernet card to connect up to a TCP/IP network for Client/
 Server operations. To send and receive GxNet telegrams via Ethernet, you will need the
 "ETHERNET" license.

title: Set up ID address
text:
Give each device in the TCP/IP network its own IP address. The IP address is split up into
 three blocks of 3 bytes each. During input, you are switched automatically to the next block
 after three digits. Use the arrow keys to access individual blocks directly in order to make
 changes or to move to the next block if you have only entered two digits.
 Do not enter duplicate IP addresses. A duplicate IP address will cause
 errors in the network. Ask your network administrator.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <IP address>
 Enter and confirm IP address.

title: Enter subnet mask
text:
Enter the subnet mask for the local network here, in which your device is integrated. The
 subnet mask has to be identical for all devices in a subnetwork.
 The subnet mask is allocated by the network administrator. This must
 not be changed at a later date. An incorrect subnet mask can cause er-
 rors in the network.
 Set up and input of the subnet mask correspond to the procedure for the IP address, see
 page 404.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Subnet mask>
 Enter the Subnet mask and confirm your input.

title: Enter gateway address
text:
The gateway address is the address of the node via which the partner can be accessed
outside of the local network.
 The gateway address is allocated by the network administrator. This
 must not be changed at a later date.
Set up and input of the gateway address correspond to the procedure for the IP address,
see page 404.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Gateway address>
 Enter and confirm gateway address.

title: Send single ping
text:
To check the Ethernet interface, you can send a single ping from your device to the higher-
ranking server. Do this by entering the IP address of the server, see page 404.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Single Ping>
 Enter and confirm IP address.
 A ping is sent to the IP address you entered. A message is issued to let you know if
 the ping was successful or not.
 Confirm message.

title: Specify the connection parameters
text:
In the connection parameter table, you determine via which physical interface (bus type)
data is sent to which device via a particular channel. Depending on the bus type you se-
lect, further specifications might be necessary. For each channel, enter first the device ID
and then the bus type.
In mode level T, softkeys can be defined for an EDP system. Pressing a key, or entering
input is then not processed by the device but sent to the EDP system. You establish the
connection for this setup via the connection parameter table as well.
For the channels A to G and for mode level T, the connection parameter table contains the
following data:
"Device ID": Device ID of connected device, e.g. 1 for EDP system. The de-
 vice ID corresponds to the system bus address.
"Bus type": Select the type of bus via which the device is connected. The
 following settings are possible:
 – "Inactive": Channel is not active.
 – "Standard system bus"
 – "PC system bus": For GxControl applications.
 – "AEDP": For an EDP connection. The EDP system always
 has system bus address 1.
 – "Storage medium": Set this if you want to use a storage
 medium to buffer system processes.
 – "TCP/IP": For an Ethernet connection (TCP/IP). Further
 specifications are required in the columns, "Port No.",
 "Synchronization" and "Conversion".
 – "USB": For the device that is connected with the channel
 via a USB connection.

text:

gle package data, the different totals and/or statistics reports are operated via these chan-
nels.

In the "Add.data to PSV_PCK" table, select the additional data you want to be transmitted
or printed with the package-synchronous data.
 The additional data that is supported can be found in the annex, see
 page 497.

total labels, allocate this data to the channel of the respective total printer.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Outgoing lines> / <Add.data to PSV_PCK>
 Allocate the data you want to the channels A to G or to the internal printer.
 Close table.

title: Select Send single package data to higher-ranking EDP sys-
text:
tem (content of PSV_DATA)
 In the "Contents of PSV_DATA" table (package-synchronous data), select the single pack-
 age data you want sent to the higher-ranking EDP system.

title: In the standard setting, only valid package data are sent to the EDP system after the pack-
text:
ages have been checked. If necessary, you can transfer the data from faulty packages, in
 respectively identified data records, see page 413.
 The transferred package data can be found in annex, see page 497.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Outgoing lines> / <Contents of PSV_DATA>
 Allocate the data you want to channels A and B.
 Close table.

title: Select Send data on change
text:
In the "Send if data is mod." table you determine which data and commands are sent to
 which channel when changed manually or via an interface.
 The available data and commands can be found in the annex, see
 page 497.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Outgoing lines> / <Send if data is mod.>
 Make settings.
 Close table.

title: Only send valid or also faulty package data to the higher-rank-
text:
ing EDP system
This is where you determine whether package-synchronous data are sent to the higher-
ranking EDP system for all packages or only for valid packages. The following settings are
possible:
"Valid": Only package-synchronous data for valid packages (PSV_DA-
 TA) are sent to the EDP system. Standard setting.
"All": The package-synchronous data for valid packages (PSV_DA-
 TA) and the package-synchronous data for faulty packages
 (PSV_ERRDATA) are also sent to the EDP system.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Outgoing lines> / <Packages f. PSV DATA>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Set receiving level for remote printing
text:
If print jobs are stored temporarily in a total printer, this is where you can set the number of
30 print jobs you want saved (receiving level). This can be necessary, if, for example, total la-
 bels for boxes are printed on a separate total printer (see picture), or if there are several
 boxes between the box machine and the total printer and "Ack. after receipt" is set as con-
 firmation type, see page 415.
 You can enter a receiving level up to a maximum of 30 (standard setting = 7). If the receiv-
 ing level is exceeded, a message is issued to the labeling machine and labeling is stop-
 ped. Once the print jobs have been completed, you can continue with labeling.
 If a labeling machine is stopped once the receiving level is reached, you
 have to restart it upon acceptance of the total labels.
 Illustration 77: Example of labeling machine with automatic box machine and total printer
 1 Automatic labeler

title: Total printer
text:
Enter these settings at the remote device.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Incoming lines> / <No. receive buffers>
 Enter and confirm the number of print jobs you want saved.

title: Set confirmation for remote printing
text:
On remotely operated devices (e.g. total printer), you can determine whether the automatic
labeler should continue with labeling after a print order has been sent. The following set-
tings are possible:
"Ack. after receipt": Labeling is continued as soon as the total printer has received
 the print job.
"Ack. after labeling": Labeling is continued as soon as the printed total label is re-
 moved from the total printer. Standard setting.
"Ack. after printout": Labeling is continued as soon as the total label has been prin-
 ted. If the total label is not removed while the next label is being
 printed, labeling is stopped until the label is removed.
 Enter these settings at the remote device.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Incoming lines> / <Acknowledge. PSV_PCK>
 Tap softkey with respective setting.

title: Set trigger for remote printing
text:
On remote-operated devices (e.g. total printer), you can determine how printing is initial-
ized. The following settings are possible:
"L.barr.": Printing is triggered by a light barrier or trigger signal. Standard
 setting.
"Immed.": Printing is started as soon as the print job has been received.
 Enter these settings at the remote device.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Incoming lines> / <Release remotePrint>
 Tap softkey with respective setting.

title: Set error message for remote printing
text:
On remotely-operated devices (e.g. total printer), you can determine whether the master
 device receives negative confirmation in the event of an error. The following settings are
 possible:
30 "ErrMsg": The master devices receives negative confirmation in the event
 of an error. "Ack. after receipt" may not be set as confirmation
 type, see page 415.
 "LOCK": The master device does not receive a message in the event of
 an error. The remote device stops and the operator is prompted
 to remove the error. Printing is repeated afterwards.
 Enter these settings at the remote device.
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Incoming lines> / <On error remotePrint>
 Tap softkey with respective setting.

title: Forward reception data from the higher-ranking EDP system to
text:
devices on the system bus
 If you activate the <Bridge> function, you can send data received by the higher-ranking
 EDP system to the respective device in a data record, via the system bus, using the re-
 spective device address. The following settings are possible:
 – "Pass.". Default setting.
 – "Active"
 A "BRIDGE" license is required.
 Mode level: 2
 <Interfaces> / <Bridge>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Creating E-mail address book
text:
Enter the name and email addresses of the people you want to send emails to in the email
address book. You can save up to five email addresses for each recipient.
Use the following shortcut to enter the special character @:
<2nd>, <Shift> and <Q>
The device is configured to send e-mails, see page 418.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Emails> / <Email addr. book>
 Recipient names such as company, department, person, etc. are entered via the dis-
 played keyboard and confirmed, e.g. "Storage".
 A table for up to 5 e-mail addresses of this recipient appears.
 Enter and confirm e-mail addresses.

title: Deleting e-mail addresses
text:
With this function you can delete all the e-mail addresses belonging to a recipient.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Emails> / <Delete email address>
 Select recipient in e-mail address book and press <OK>.
 To delete a recipient's e-mail addresses completely, answer the security check with
 "yes".

title: E-mail configuration
text:
To send e-mails, the device has to be configured appropriately, see page 418. Configura-
 tion is usually handled by Bizerba Service.
 The configuration table contains the following entries:
30 "Protocol": – "SMTP": E-mail function is activated with SMTP protocol.
 Further entries are required in the following four table rows.
 – "off": E-mail function is deactivated. The following four ta-
 ble rows are blocked against input.
 "Own email address": Enter your own e-mail address.
 "Post-out server Enter the IP address of the post output server (ask system ad-
 (SMTP)": ministrator).
 "SMTP Port": Enter the SMTP port address (ask system administrator).
 "Authentication": As the device only sends e-mails, but cannot receive any, the
 post input server (POP3) is only for authentication. If e-mails
 cannot be sent via SMTP, an attempt is made to authenticate
 the procedure by POP3. Next, the device tries again to send the
 e-mail by SMTP. The following settings are possible:
 – "no": no authentication by POP3. The following four table
 rows are blocked against input.
 – "POP3/SMTP-Plain": Authentication by POP3 is activated.
 Further entries are required in the following four table rows.
 "Post-in server (POP3)": Enter IP address of post input server (ask system administra-
 tor).
 "POP3 Port": Enter POP3 port address (ask system administrator).
 "User name": Only in the event of an

title: Send e-mail
text:
The device is configured to send e-mails, see page 418.
The email address book is not empty.
Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Ethernet> / <Emails> / <Send email>
 Select the recipient using the cursor keys.
or
 Enter the name of the recipient.
 Press <OK>.
 Enter the e-mail subject line.
or
 Search for saved text, see page 419.
 Press <Next>.
 Enter the e-mail text.
or
 Search for saved text, see page 419.
 Press <Send email>.
The device sends the e-mail.

title: Finding saved text for e-mail
text:
The editor for the e-mail subject line or e-mail text is open.
 Press <Load>.
 Enter text number and confirm, see page 77.
The text appears in the editor.

title: Activate or deactivate transmission channels
text:
The following transmission channels in the device can be switched on or off, completely
independently of one another:
– <Send channel A>
– <Send channel B>
– <Send channel C>
– <Send channel D>
– <Send channel E>
– <Internal printing> (transmission channel for internal printer)
Assignment of transmission channels is handled individually for each customer, see
page 406.
 Application example: This function enables you to close the connection, for example, to
 a higher-ranking EDP system by switching off the respective transmission channel. You
 can operate the device afterwards independently.
 Mode level: 2
30 <Printer + interface> / <Send chan. active?>
 Tap the softkey for the transmission channel you want to either switch on or off until
 the setting you require is visible.

title: Select year formatting via interface
text:
You can choose in how many digits the year number is transmitted and printed. The fol-
 lowing settings are possible:
 – "2-digit". Default setting.
 – "4-digit"
 Mode level: 5
 <Interfaces> / <Etc> / <Year via interf.>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Package guidance
text:
The device may be equipped with an adjustable package guidance (alignment rails). Un-
der certain circumstances, packages of critical dimensions must be laterally guided during
transport to avoid toppling over. For this reason, optional package guidances can be
mounted onto the conveyor belts.

title: Manual package guidance
text:
In case of different package sizes the alignment rails of the package guidance need to be
adjusted to the package sizes accordingly. The distance between the alignment rails
should be slightly larger than the package width.

title: Centered package alignment
text:
With the two-part conveyor belts usually a centered package alignment is used.
Illustration 78: Centered package guidance
When changing the package with the alignment rails A and B need to be moved by the
same value from the center.
Proceed as follows:
 Loosen star handle 1 .
 Move the front and back alignment rail forward or back by the same distancee middle
 axis.
 Tighten star handles 1 .

title: Lateral package guidance
text:
For lateral package guidance the alignment rail is pre-set and the alignment rail is set ac-
 cordingly to the package width.
31
 Illustration 79: Lateral package guidance
 When changing the package width the alignment rail B must be set.
 Proceed as follows:
 Loosen star handles 1 .
 Move alignment rail B by respective distance.
 Tighten star handles 1 .

title: Motorized guide rails
text:
The device may be equipped with motorized guide rails. They allow easy and fast adjust-
 ment of the alignment rails to the respective aperture width according to different package
 or article sizes.

title: Switching on/off motorized guide rails
text:
The following settings are possible:
 – "W/o"
 – "With"
 Mode level: 5
 <Automat> / <Optional equipment> / <Powered guide rails>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Defining operating mode of guide rails
text:
The following operating modes are available for the motorized guide rails:
"One-sid." The outer guide rail remains fixed. To adjust the relative pack-
 age width, only one guide rail is moved by means of a motor.
"Symet." Both guide rails are moved symmetrically. This allows centered
 package guidance on the conveyor belts.
Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Guiding rails> / <Calibration guid. rails> / <Oper. mode guid. rail>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Specifying the maximum package width
text:
Here you may specify the max. package width. Depending on this specification, it is impos-
sible to enter greater values in mode level 2, 3 or 4.
Mode level: 5
 <Automat> / <Transport equipment> / <Max. package width>
 Enter and confirm the max. package width in mm.

title: Entering the package width
text:
Here you may enter the package width for motorized guide rail adjustment or modify a
 package width called up with the PLU or automatic labeler data. If package width is man-
 aged in the automatic labeler data, the entered value can be saved in the database if re-
 quired.

title: If the package width is specified in the automatic labeler data, the pack-
text:
age width of the associated automatic labeler data is set at PLU
 change.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Guiding rails> / <Package width>
 Enter the max. package width in mm.
 To save the value in automatic labeler data, activate the "->Database [Etc]" field.
 If the field is not activated, the value is only used for the current labeling job.
 Press <OK>.
 Input area:
 Min.: 78 mm
 Max.: Depends on the specifications in mode level 5.
 When entering values outside these parameters, a message containing
 the valid range is displayed.

title: Automatic guide rail adjustment via softkeys
text:
If necessary, the guide rails can be manually adjusted to the relevant aperture width using
 the <Guid. rails ON> and <Guid. rails OFF>softkeys.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Guiding rails>
 Call up guide rail adjustment:
 <Guid. rails ON> Increase aperture width of guide rails.
 <Guid. rails OFF> Decrease aperture width of guide rails.
 <Guid. rails STOP> Stop adjustment after reaching the corresponding position.
 After stopping motorized guide rail adjustment, the set position is displayed in the
 <Package width> softkey.

title: Guide rail adjustment
text:
The motorized guide rails can be adjusted using a tilt lever. The front and rear guide rail
can be adjusted separately.
The rear guide rail is adjusted using the tilt lever A, the front guide rail is adjusted using
the tilt lever B.
Illustration 80: Adjusting guide rails
Motorized guide rail adjustment by means of the tilt levers A and B can be defined as fol-
lows:
 Illustration 81: Lever position
Motorized adjustment of the guide rail: Tilt lever in position 1 .
This position allows adjusting the respective guide rail either automatically according to
PLU data, manually via softkeys or according to the specified package width.
Manual guide rail adjustment: Tilt lever in position 2 .
This position allows adjusting the respective guide rail by manually moving it to a position
that suits the package width.
 After manually adjusting the guide rail, bring titling lever back to position
 1 .
 Without guide rail adjustment: Tilt lever in position 3 .
 In case of lateral alignment of packages, see page 422, one guide rail is fixed and the oth-
31 er one's position is changed by means of a motor. In doing so, the fixed guide rail can be
 blocked against motorized and manual adjustment by bringing the tilt lever into position
 3 .

title: Removing motorized guide rails
text:
The motorized guide rails can be removed and remounted in order to clean the guide rails
themselves or conveyor belts and belt units.
Illustration 82: Remove guide rails
Removing guide rails:
– Take hold of the star handles 1 with both hands and remove complete guide rail
 from the mounting 2 pulling it upwards in direction of the arrow.
– Clean guide rail and belt units, see page 377.
Repositioning guide rails:
– Take hold of the star handles 1 with both hands and insert complete guide rail into
 the mounting 2 downwards in direction of the arrow. Make sure that the driving pins
 of the guide rails 3 engage in the guide rail plate.
– Depending on the operating mode, automatically adjust one or both guide rails via the
 corresponding softkeys, see page 424, and check correct positioning of the guide
 rails.

title: Guide rail calibration
text:
First calibration or re-calibration of the motorized guide rails is necessary in the following
 cases:
 – At first commissioning of the device.
 – After adjustment of the fixed guide rail.
31 – If the device was switched off during device adjustment.
 – If movement was blocked during device adjustment.
 The following steps are required for calibration:
 1. Move guide rails manually to obtain the greatest aperture width.
 2. Fix one rail or engage both tilting levers.
 3. Selection of operating mode.
 4. Enter measured aperture width using the <Calibrate aper.width> softkey.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Guiding rails> / <Calibration guid. rails> / <Calibrate aper.width>
 Enter measured aperture width in mm.
 Press <OK>.

title: Activating or deactivating metal detectors
text:
If the device is equipped with a metal detector, the latter can be activated or deactivated
 here. The following settings are possible:
 – "With"
 – "W/o". Default setting.
 Mode level: 5
 <Automat> / <Optional equipment> / <Metal detector>
 Tap the softkey until the required setting is highlighted.

title: Entering the metal detector product number manually
text:
The device can save product-specific parameters of the metal detector under a product
 number. The product number is usually stored in the article data and called up together
 with the PLU. Here you can enter the product number manually. This is required if the
 product number is not included in the PLU data.
 Mode level: 1
 <Device menu> / <Etc> / <Metal detector product no.>
 Enter value and confirm input.

title: Operating the metal detector
text:
Metal detectors generate strong magnetic fields.
 DANGER The magnetic field of the metal detector affects cardiac pacemak-
 ers! Mortal danger!
 The pacemaker sends no or incorrect impulses.
 – Persons with pacemakers must not stay near a metal detector.
The device may be equipped with an optional metal detector to detect and eject packages
containing metals. You will receive separate operating instructions for the metal detector.
 Refer to the operating instructions to familiarize yourself with the opera-
 tion and possible risks before using the metal detector.

title: Package ejector
text:
A package ejector can be mounted at the end of the transport unit to eject packages.
Depending on the specification, packages can be ejected for the following reasons, see
page 267:
– Eject overweight or underweight packages, see page 326.
– Eject packages containing metal (only in connection with metal detector).
– Eject packages when total preselection is reached.
– Eject incorrect or unlabeled packages (only in connection with code check unit), see
 page 456.
– Eject packages in the event of malfunctions (e.g. at end of label roll).
– Eject packages after switching to conveying mode, see page 356.

title: Package ejector description
text:
The flaps of the package ejector that are provided with transport rollers are controlled
 pneumatically by means of compressed air cylinders. For this reason, the package ejector
 is connected to the compressed air supply of the device. The permissible max. force at the
 flaps of the package ejector is 75 N.
31
 Illustration 83: View: package ejector

title: Maximum package size
text:
The open flaps of the package ejector have a clearance height of approx. 190 mm and a
 clear width of approx. 300 mm. Thus, packages with maximum dimensions up to the said
 ones can be ejected in a safe and reliable way.
 Package height Package width Package length
 180 mm 300 mm 500 mm

title: Settings
text:
The following settings can be made for the package ejector:
– Polarity, see page 266
– Activation criteria, see page 267
– Delay time, see page 268
– Parameter of control and container light barrier, see page 268
– Air pressure at pressure reducer
 CAUTION Pressure of compressed air of the pusher too high!
 Risk of injury due to a too high force at the flaps of the package
 ejector.
 – Check permissible pressure of compressed air. The permissible
 pressure is indicated on a plate at the pressure reducing valve.

title: Pusher for package ejection
text:
A pusher can be mounted at the end of the transport unit. It is used to eject or divert pack-
ages prior to further conveying.
Illustration 84: View: Pusher
 1 Clamping lever

title: Adjusting pusher lengthwise to conveying direction
text:
The pusher can be moved lengthwise to the conveying direction. To do so, loosen the four
 fastening screws 2 , move the pusher to the desired position and tighten the screws.

title: Adjusting pusher at right angles to the conveying belt
text:
In the event of considerable differences in package size, the pusher can be moved at right
31 angles to the conveying belt. Thanks to a piston position near the package, short ejection
 times become possible. Unblock the two clamping levers 1 , move the pusher close to the
 package to be ejected and block clamping levers again.

title: Compressed air supply for pusher
text:
The pusher has a separate pressure reducer 3 that is directly mounted to the pusher
 mounting unit. Set the relevant air pressure depending on package size using the manom-
 eter. In versions without automatic outlet, the accumulated condensed water has to be
 drained off, if necessary. The max. force of the pusher is 75 N.
 CAUTION Pressure of compressed air of the pusher too high!
 Risk of injury through strong push from pusher.
 – Check permissible pressure of compressed air. The permissible
 pressure is indicated on a plate at the pressure reducing valve.
 The filter element of the pressure reducer has to be controlled at regular
 intervals and changed in case of heavy soiling.

title: Swivel-mounted labeling conveyor for long packages
text:
To label packages that are longer than the weighing belt, the device can be provided with
 a swivel-mounted labeling belt. Thus, packages with a length up to 700 mm can be weigh-
 ed.
 The product may not bend and touch the swiveled-down belt. If it touch-
 es the swiveled-down belt, the measured weight is falsified.
Illustration 85: Swiveling down the labeling conveyor in the event of long packages
 1 Weighing conveyor

title: Swivel-mounted labeling conveyor
text:
If during transport, a package 2 longer than 500 mm is detected on the infeed and sepa-
ration belt, the labeling belt end near the weighing belt 1 is pneumatically swiveled down.
Thus, the overlapping part of the package does not touch the labeling belt 4 and the
package can be weighed. After weighing, the swiveled-down labeling belt is lifted and the
package is transported to the labeler.
Required settings
The swivel-mounted labeling conveyor has to activated by the Bizerba service once. To be
able to work with the swivel-mounted conveyor, the weighing belt has to be set to the
<Weighing Start/Stop> operating mode, see page 264.

title: V belts
text:
The device can be equipped with optional V belts. V belts are oblique adjustable conveyor
belts that allow safe transport of bulky and difficult products such as cabbage, salad, chick-
en etc.
 The V belts of the device have to be activated by the Bizerba service once.
31
 Illustration 86: V belt, side view
 1 Adjustment unit with crank handle

title: Back part of V belt
text:
The belt inclination of the front 2 and back 4 part of the V belt can be individually adjus-
 ted. For this reason, each V belt is provided with two adjustment units 1 :
 – Left adjustment unit for inclination of V belt front part 2
 – Right adjustment unit for inclination of V belt back part 4

title: Oblique adjustment of V belts
text:
The optimal inclination of V belts depends on the product. Find out the best adjustment by
performing tests with the product to be labeled.

title: Crank
text:
Illustration 87: Adjustment unit of V belt
 Press <Stop>.
 The conveyor belts stop.
 Adjust inclination of both parts of one V belt by rotating the cranks 2 of both adjust-
 ment units.
 Read the belt inclination of the front and back V belt at the indicator field 1 of the
 respective adjustment unit.
 Set all back parts and all front parts of the V belt to the same values respectively by
 means of the indicator field 1 .
 Start the device via <Start> and perform a test run with the product to be labeled.
 Repeat operation until a satisfactory result is obtained.
 After V belt inclination, check labeler height adjustment and correct it, if necessary,
 see page 45.

title: Label pressure roller
text:
The label pressure roller can be fastened to the labeler in three different positions. Thus,
the label can be pressed on during transport on the belt independently from conveying di-
rection and labeler rotation. Labels stick better to film-wrapped packages which are slightly
curved due to overpressure during packaging in modified atmosphere.
Thanks to its oscillating suspension, the label pressure roller is lifted by the transported
package. After pressing on the label, the label pressure roller returns to its starting posi-
tion. Since oscillation is limited, the labeler and the label pressure roller have to be adjus-
ted to the respective package height to apply sufficient pressure.
 The pressure of the label pressure roller can be increased by inserting washers. Up to
 three mounting rails can be mounted (see figure on the left). If the labeler position
 changes, the label pressure roller can be fastened to one of the mounting rails depending
 on the labeler position. Only one label pressure roller can be mounted at the required posi-
 tion.
31
 Illustration 88: View: pressure roller
 Applications
 The label pressure roller is only suitable for top labeling of almost even or slightly curved
 surfaces with little height difference between the individual packages.

title: Label dispenser
text:
If a label dispenser is mounted to the con-
 veyor unit of the device, it can be used to
 apply preprinted labels to the packages.
 Possible use
 Additional application of the following labels
 to packages:
 – Decorative labels
 – Campaign labels
 – Other preprinted labels
 Illustration 89: View: label dispenser
Label dispenser components
 1 Guide disk

title: Label roll
text:
Illustration 90: Components
 The label dispenser can be configured by means of a formula sent by
 the device at first commissioning or when labels of a different size are
 used. If required, the Bizerba service will program and configure the de-
 vice accordingly.

title: Inserting the label roll
text:
Before inserting a new label roll, set the label dispenser to "PAUSE" or
 switch it off using the mains switch.
31
 Illustration 91: Insert label roll
 Remove the outside guide disk 1 .
 Insert the new label roll 13 with labels facing outside.
 Feed label strip around auxiliary rolls 3 and dancer arms of unwind unit 2 .
 Reattach the outside guide disk 1 .
 Swivel dancer arm 4 away from the auxiliary roll 5 .
 Feed label strip past the auxiliary roll 5 , pass it between the auxiliary rolls 6 ,
 through the light barrier 7 to the dispenser tongue 9 .
 Place dancer arm 4 again on the auxiliary roll 5 .
 Pull the label strip until it reaches the take-up pin 12 .
 Remove labels 8 from the backing paper that protrudes beyond the dispenser
 tongue 9 .
 Feed label strip around dispenser tongue and pass it through the auxiliary rolls 6 to
 the draw roller 10 .
 Lift the counterpressure roll 11 and pass the label strip between the draw roller 10
 and the counterpressure roll 11 .
 Feed the label strip past the counterpressure roll 11 to the take-up pin 12 and pass it
 between the rods.
 Press <START – STOP> to register the new label roll.
 If the label strip moves obliquely, adjust the lateral control (guide ring) in parallel.
 If no label is dispensed after activating the start key, check whether the
 label strip has been fed through the light barrier 7 and the light barrier
 detects t

title: Specifications for the label dispenser
text:
Specifications for the label dispenser are made via the display and operating unit.
31
 Illustration 92: Display and operating unit
 Key functions
 <START – STOP>
 This key is used to switch on or off the device. In the subme-
 nus, a test dispensing process can be activated by pressing this
 key. This key may also be used to confirm a label roll change.
 <MODE – ENTER>
 This key has two functions:
 When the MODE line is displayed, you may switch between
 "READY" and "PAUSE".
 When calling up or saving label settings, this key is used to call
 up or save a current label number.
 <DOWN>
 This key is used to change between the label parameters.
 <UP>
 This key is used to change between the label parameters.
 <+>
 This key is used to change the relevant parameters.
 <->
 This key is used to change the relevant parameters.

title: Display
text:
The display shows the various parameters and the status. After switching on, the program
version number and program date are displayed.
This function disappears after a few sec-
onds or can be deleted by confirming it us-
ing a key.
 Illustration 93: Version and date
The displayed standard text is the MODE text. The status of the label dispenser, the num-
ber of dispensed labels and the current program number are displayed here.
Switch between the parameters by pressing
the <UP> or <DOWN> keys.
 Illustration 94: Standard text
Changing the mode
The label dispenser can be operated in different modes. Change the mode by pressing the
<MODE – ENTER> key.
The following modes are available:
– "READY"
– "PAUSE"
 Illustration 95: Change mode
"READY" The label dispenser emits a label when the product sensor is
 activated.
"PAUSE" The label dispenser does not emit any label when the product
 sensor is activated.
 If the label dispenser is set to the "PAUSE" mode, use the
 <START – STOP> key to activate it.
If a system is provided with two label dispensers, the "STANDBY" mode is also available.
The label dispenser in "STANDBY" mode is designed as redundant system and remains in
"STANDBY" mode until the other label dispenser reports error. In the event of an error, the
label dispenser in "STANDBY" mode is automatically set to "READY".

title: Error messages
text:
The label dispenser automatically generates an error message at label roll end.
 After inserting the new label roll, press the
 <START – STOP> key until the label dis-
 penser changes to the "READY" mode.

title: Setting label parameters
text:
Label positioning
This parameter determines the label posi-
tion on the package. Change this value by
pressing the <+> or <-> key.
 Illustration 97: Label positioning
If the product sensor is located at 100 mm in front of the dispenser tongue and the label
shall be placed at a distance of 37.5 mm from the product leading edge, the value must be
137.5 mm. If the product sensor setting refers to the product trailing edge, the product
length has to be deducted from the value to be entered.
 This value depends on the belt speed. If belt speed is not correctly set,
 label positioning is incorrect too.
Label protrusion

tion on the dispenser tongue. Change this

title: Writing unit for RFID labels
text:
With the label printer, optionally, data can be transmitted to RFID labels (RFID = Radio
 Frequency Identification, or: Smart Label). This is currently only possible for RFID labels
 with UHF transponders.
 When purchasing RFID labels, ask Bizerba Service which RFID labels
 types have been tested by Bizerba.
 Labels with UHF transponders
 UHF labels have a semi-conductor chip incorporated in special positions that transmit and
 receive in a frequency range of 865-920 MHz. The memory's capacity is 12 byte (96 bit).
 The label may not be printed where the semi-conductor chip is located.
 Specifications when processing RFID labels
 When processing RFID labels, you need the following functions:
 – Activate Smart Label, see page 392
 – Create code structure rule, see page 215
 – Select code field for smart label, see page 231

title: Tendency control
text:
The tendency control function requires the "TENDENCY CONTROL" li-
 cense.
 The tendency control is used to control a customer-side dosing, transporting or slicing de-
 vice in relation to the statistical mean value of the weighed packages. Any deviations to
 the mean value can be corrected directly via outputs.
 Enter the required specifications in tables. These tables are assigned to articles via the pa-
 rameter numbers.
The following functions are available:
– Define or edit tendency control parameter tables, see page 454
– Delete tendency control parameter tables, see page 455
– Directly call up tendency control parameter tables, see page 455
– Edit tendency control parameters for the current labeling job, see page 455

title: Principle of the tendency control
text:
The mean value is continuously calculated via the "Number of Pckg. for mean value" that
 is entered. If the calculated mean value exceeds the "Tolerance +" or falls below the "Tol-
 erance -", a control factor is calculated and output.
 After sending the control factor, the package number entered under "Neutral path" is ignor-
 ed. Afterwards, a mean value is formed from the following packages. After starting the
31 dosing device, a mean value is calculated once the number of packages has been entered
 under "Start delay".

title: Overview of tendency control parameters
text:
The following overview shows all the possible attributes in a tendency
 control parameter table. Which attributes can actually be managed in
 your tendency control parameter tables depends on how the database
 is configured.
 The configuration of the database is not subject of this documentation.
 Please contact your Bizerba consultant or Bizerba Service for further in-
 formation.
 "Target weight": The package weight that should be attained with the help of the
 tendency control. Depending on the filling system, the target
 weight may be greater or smaller than the nominal weight.
 "Number of Pckg. for Number of packages whose weight is used to calculate the
 mean value": mean value for regulating the control device.
 "Upper limit", "Lower lim- Packages not within the specified upper and lower limit are not
 it": used to calculate the mean value (outliers).
 "Tolerance +", "Toler- If the mean value of the package weight is within this tolerance
 ance -": range, the tendency control is not applied.
 "Start delay": Number of packages that are not used to calculate the mean
 value once the process has been started.
 "Neutral path": Number of packages that are not used to calculate the mean
 value after regulation has been applied.
 "Ctrl factor": Specification which signal the control device requires to change
 the mean value, e. g. by 1 g.
